# Introduction

**Purpose**

This notebook develops and compares models that rank Home Credit applicants by the risk of payment difficulty. Its immediate objective is to outperform a simple benchmark on out-of-sample ROC-AUC and produce evidence that can support the business problem. `TARGET = 1` is described as observed payment difficulty, not as a regulatory definition of default.

The modeling design follows the [data map](../01_data_map.qmd), [industry context](../02_industry_context.qmd), [EDA plan](../03_eda_plan.qmd), and completed [data preparation](02_data_preparation.qmd). It establishes the modeling contract, compares candidate algorithms, evaluates imbalance strategies, tunes and validates XGBoost, fits the selected model, and produces a submission-ready test score file.

## Modeling design contract

The earlier project work creates the following constraints for modeling:

| Design area | Modeling rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Unit of analysis | Keep one row per current applicant. | Data map |
| Outcome | Predict `TARGET`, interpreted as payment difficulty. | Data map and EDA plan |
| Identifiers | Use `SK_ID_CURR` for alignment and auditing, never as a predictor. | Data map and EDA plan |
| Timing | Use only information available when the current application was evaluated. | EDA plan |
| Historical behavior | Exclude future realized payments, balances, terminations, and reporting updates. | EDA plan |
| Missing history | Keep no history, unmeasured history, and no measured delinquency as distinct states. | EDA findings |
| Governance | Do not promote sensitive or proxy fields to predictors without fairness and policy review. | Industry context and EDA findings |
| Population shift | Apply transformations learned from training data unchanged to the scoring population. | EDA plan |
| Primary metric | Compare models using out-of-sample ROC-AUC; report accuracy only as a secondary metric. | Industry context and EDA plan |
| Validation | Use stratified 3-fold cross-validation during exploration. | Modeling assignment |
| Business decisions | Do not select an approval threshold or claim an approval-rate lift without decision costs and the relevant applicant population. | Industry context and EDA plan |

ROC-AUC of 0.79 is retained as a project performance target that must be validated. It is not treated as a universal industry standard. Model discrimination also does not by itself establish an appropriate approval threshold.

# Section 1: Setup and prepared-data audit

## Reproducible setup

The audit reads the RDS outputs from data preparation because they preserve R column types exactly. The Parquet copies remain available for interoperability. A fixed seed is recorded now and will be reused when resamples and tuning candidates are generated in later sections.

```{r}
#| label: setup

required_packages <- c("knitr", "digest")

missing_packages <- required_packages[
  !vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]

if (length(missing_packages) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Install the following package(s) before rendering: ",
    paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

model_seed <- 20261008L
set.seed(model_seed)

modeling_run_mode <- tolower(Sys.getenv("MODELING_RUN_MODE", "development"))
if (!modeling_run_mode %in% c("development", "final")) {
  stop("MODELING_RUN_MODE must be either 'development' or 'final'.")
}

# Recorded after uploading outputs/submission.csv to Kaggle.
kaggle_public_score <- 0.76189
kaggle_private_score <- 0.75758

root_candidates <- c(".", "..")
project_root <- root_candidates[
  file.exists(file.path(root_candidates, "data", "processed", "train_prepared.rds"))
][1]

if (is.na(project_root)) {
  stop(
    "Could not locate data/processed/train_prepared.rds from the current working directory."
  )
}

processed_dir <- file.path(project_root, "data", "processed")
result_cache_dir <- file.path(project_root, "outputs", "modeling_results")
dir.create(result_cache_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

analysis_cache_version <- "2026-10-09-runtime-v3"
analysis_signature <- paste(
  analysis_cache_version,
  file.info(c(
    file.path(project_root, "R", "modeling_functions.R"),
    file.path(project_root, "R", "modeling_recipes.R"),
    file.path(processed_dir, "train_modeling_base.rds")
  ))$mtime,
  sep = "|",
  collapse = "|"
)

cached_modeling_result <- function(
    name,
    code,
    spec_signature,
    required_artifacts = character()) {
  cache_path <- file.path(result_cache_dir, paste0(name, ".rds"))
  cache_signature <- digest::digest(list(
    analysis = analysis_signature,
    specification = spec_signature
  ))
  artifacts_available <-
    !length(required_artifacts) || all(file.exists(required_artifacts))
  if (identical(modeling_run_mode, "development") &&
      file.exists(cache_path) && artifacts_available) {
    cached <- readRDS(cache_path)
    if (identical(cached$signature, cache_signature)) {
      return(cached$value)
    }
  }

  value <- force(code)
  saveRDS(
    list(signature = cache_signature, value = value),
    cache_path,
    compress = FALSE
  )
  value
}

detected_cores <- parallel::detectCores(logical = FALSE)
if (is.na(detected_cores)) detected_cores <- 1L
requested_workers <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(Sys.getenv("MODELING_WORKERS", "1")))
if (is.na(requested_workers) || requested_workers < 1L) requested_workers <- 1L
parallel_workers <- min(requested_workers, max(1L, detected_cores - 1L))
modeling_cluster <- NULL
if (parallel_workers > 1L &&
    requireNamespace("doParallel", quietly = TRUE) &&
    requireNamespace("foreach", quietly = TRUE)) {
  modeling_cluster <- parallel::makePSOCKcluster(parallel_workers)
  doParallel::registerDoParallel(modeling_cluster)
}
resample_engine_threads <- if (is.null(modeling_cluster)) 4L else 1L
required_files <- c(
  "train_prepared.rds",
  "test_prepared.rds",
  "predictor_names.rds",
  "prep_recipe.rds"
)

missing_files <- required_files[
  !file.exists(file.path(processed_dir, required_files))
]

if (length(missing_files) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Missing required prepared-data file(s): ",
    paste(missing_files, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

train_prepared <- readRDS(file.path(processed_dir, "train_prepared.rds"))
test_prepared <- readRDS(file.path(processed_dir, "test_prepared.rds"))
predictor_names <- readRDS(file.path(processed_dir, "predictor_names.rds"))

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  fig.align = "center",
  out.width = "85%"
)

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    setting = c("Run mode", "Parallel resample workers", "Threads per resample fit"),
    value = c(modeling_run_mode, parallel_workers, resample_engine_threads)
  ),
  caption = "Modeling runtime configuration"
)
```

Only the compact audit results are displayed below. The large prepared tables are not printed.

The notebook defaults to `development` mode. Completed expensive resampling results are loaded from `outputs/modeling_results` when their code-and-data signature matches. Set the `MODELING_RUN_MODE` environment variable to `final` for a clean final render that recomputes and refreshes every saved result. Full-data fits default to one resample worker with four engine threads because concurrent folds were memory-bound on this machine; `MODELING_WORKERS` can raise the resample-worker count on a higher-memory system. In either mode, the required comparisons still use stratified 3-fold cross-validation, and tuning still evaluates 20 configurations on the approximately 5,000-row tuning sample.

## Applicant grain and target separation

The data map requires one row per `SK_ID_CURR`, with `TARGET` available only for model development. The checks below stop the notebook if that grain or separation has been broken.

```{r}
#| label: audit-grain-target

grain_checks <- c(
  "Training ID is present" = "SK_ID_CURR" %in% names(train_prepared),
  "Test ID is present" = "SK_ID_CURR" %in% names(test_prepared),
  "Training IDs are complete" = !anyNA(train_prepared$SK_ID_CURR),
  "Test IDs are complete" = !anyNA(test_prepared$SK_ID_CURR),
  "Training IDs are unique" = !anyDuplicated(train_prepared$SK_ID_CURR),
  "Test IDs are unique" = !anyDuplicated(test_prepared$SK_ID_CURR),
  "Train and test IDs do not overlap" =
    length(intersect(train_prepared$SK_ID_CURR, test_prepared$SK_ID_CURR)) == 0,
  "TARGET is present in training" = "TARGET" %in% names(train_prepared),
  "TARGET is absent from test" = !"TARGET" %in% names(test_prepared),
  "TARGET contains only 0 and 1" =
    setequal(sort(unique(train_prepared$TARGET)), c(0, 1))
)

if (!all(grain_checks)) {
  stop(
    "Prepared-data grain/target audit failed: ",
    paste(names(grain_checks)[!grain_checks], collapse = "; ")
  )
}

population_summary <- data.frame(
  population = c("Training", "Test"),
  applicants = c(nrow(train_prepared), nrow(test_prepared)),
  columns = c(ncol(train_prepared), ncol(test_prepared)),
  target_available = c("Yes", "No")
)

knitr::kable(
  population_summary,
  caption = "Prepared modeling populations",
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
)
```

The prepared populations retain the applicant-level grain. The one-column difference is expected because `TARGET` belongs only to training.

## Predictor manifest and train/test compatibility

The prepared tables contain predictors together with the applicant ID, governance-audit fields, and a quality-check field. The saved predictor manifest is therefore the authoritative allow-list. Selecting every field except `TARGET` would incorrectly introduce excluded fields into a model.

```{r}
#| label: audit-predictor-manifest

non_predictor_train <- setdiff(
  names(train_prepared),
  c(predictor_names, "TARGET")
)

schema_checks <- c(
  "Predictor names are unique" = !anyDuplicated(predictor_names),
  "Every predictor is in training" = all(predictor_names %in% names(train_prepared)),
  "Every predictor is in test" = all(predictor_names %in% names(test_prepared)),
  "ID is excluded from predictors" = !"SK_ID_CURR" %in% predictor_names,
  "TARGET is excluded from predictors" = !"TARGET" %in% predictor_names,
  "Train/test columns differ only by TARGET" = setequal(
    setdiff(names(train_prepared), "TARGET"),
    names(test_prepared)
  ),
  "Predictor classes match" = identical(
    vapply(train_prepared[predictor_names], class, character(1)),
    vapply(test_prepared[predictor_names], class, character(1))
  ),
  "Training predictors are complete" = !anyNA(train_prepared[predictor_names]),
  "Test predictors are complete" = !anyNA(test_prepared[predictor_names])
)

if (!all(schema_checks)) {
  stop(
    "Prepared-data predictor/schema audit failed: ",
    paste(names(schema_checks)[!schema_checks], collapse = "; ")
  )
}

role_summary <- data.frame(
  role = c("Predictor", "Identifier / audit / quality check", "Outcome"),
  training_columns = c(length(predictor_names), length(non_predictor_train), 1L),
  modeling_use = c(
    "Candidate model inputs",
    "Alignment, subgroup audit, or data-quality review only",
    "Observed training outcome"
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  role_summary,
  caption = "Prepared columns by modeling role"
)
```

This separation preserves the EDA's conservative treatment of gender, age, family structure, occupation, organization, education, housing, and geography. These fields remain available for later subgroup auditing but are not silently admitted as model inputs.

## Target prevalence and imbalance

```{r}
#| label: audit-target-prevalence

target_count <- table(
  factor(
    train_prepared$TARGET,
    levels = c(0, 1),
    labels = c("No observed payment difficulty", "Observed payment difficulty")
  )
)

target_summary <- data.frame(
  outcome = names(target_count),
  applicants = as.integer(target_count),
  share = as.integer(target_count) / sum(target_count)
)

knitr::kable(
  target_summary,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Training outcome distribution",
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
)
```

The positive class represents about 8% of training applicants, consistent with the EDA. A majority-class classifier will therefore appear strong on accuracy while providing no useful risk ranking. Later sections will report its accuracy and ROC-AUC explicitly, then compare candidate models primarily on cross-validated ROC-AUC.

## Application and supplementary feature coverage

The data map and preparation notebook identify the following decision-time-safe historical feature families. This audit confirms that each planned family is represented in the predictor manifest without displaying hundreds of individual columns.

```{r}
#| label: audit-feature-families

feature_family_patterns <- list(
  "Bureau credit history" = "^(bureau_|has_bureau$)",
  "Previous applications" = "^(prev_|has_previous_application$)",
  "Installment behavior" = "^(inst_|has_installments$)",
  "POS/CASH history" = "^(pos_|has_pos$)",
  "Credit-card history" = "^has_credit_card$",
  "Cross-source coverage" =
    "^(has_unmatched_history$|sources_present$|no_history_any_source$)"
)

family_counts <- vapply(
  feature_family_patterns,
  function(pattern) sum(grepl(pattern, predictor_names)),
  integer(1)
)

if (any(family_counts == 0)) {
  stop(
    "One or more expected supplementary feature families are absent: ",
    paste(names(family_counts)[family_counts == 0], collapse = "; ")
  )
}

supplementary_predictors <- unique(unlist(lapply(
  feature_family_patterns,
  function(pattern) grep(pattern, predictor_names, value = TRUE)
)))

feature_family_summary <- data.frame(
  feature_set = c(names(family_counts), "Application and engineered application fields"),
  predictors = c(
    unname(family_counts),
    length(setdiff(predictor_names, supplementary_predictors))
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  feature_family_summary,
  caption = "Candidate predictors by source family"
)
```

The family labels describe provenance, not guaranteed value. A later controlled comparison will test whether the supplementary history improves out-of-sample ROC-AUC over application-only predictors.

## Validation design and leakage boundary

Model exploration will use one shared set of stratified 3-fold resamples so candidate algorithms are compared on the same assessment applicants. ROC-AUC will be the selection metric; accuracy and other diagnostic measures can supplement it but will not replace it.

The saved prepared tables were produced by a recipe fitted to the entire training population. That is appropriate for fitting a final selected model and scoring the test population, but it is **not** the correct input for cross-validation: medians, percentile caps, quantile bins, category levels, dummy encoding, and zero-variance decisions would already contain information from each assessment fold. Before candidate-model comparison, the modeling pipeline must make those learned steps part of each resample so they are estimated on the analysis fold only.

The following validation contract will govern later sections:

1. Create stratified 3-fold splits from the training outcome.
2. Use the same folds for every candidate model and feature-set comparison.
3. Estimate all learned preprocessing from each analysis fold only.
4. Apply the fitted fold preprocessing unchanged to its assessment fold.
5. Apply sampling methods such as SMOTE only to analysis-fold data, never to assessment data.
6. Compare candidates on mean cross-validated ROC-AUC and retain fold-level results to show variability.
7. Use the test population only after model selection; do not use it for tuning or model comparison.

Section 1 establishes a valid modeling population and a validation boundary consistent with the earlier project work. No model has been trained in this section.

# Section 2: Reusable modeling functions and resamples

**Purpose**

Candidate models must be compared using the same outcome definition, folds, and metrics. This section moves those rules into reusable functions rather than repeating slightly different code for each algorithm. The functions live in `R/modeling_functions.R`, while this notebook explains and verifies their use.

This section creates resamples but does not fit a model. Fold-safe feature preprocessing remains a requirement for the next section.

## Modeling infrastructure

```{r}
#| label: load-modeling-functions

infrastructure_packages <- c("dplyr", "rlang", "rsample", "yardstick")
missing_infrastructure_packages <- infrastructure_packages[
  !vapply(
    infrastructure_packages,
    requireNamespace,
    logical(1),
    quietly = TRUE
  )
]

if (length(missing_infrastructure_packages) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Install the following modeling package(s): ",
    paste(missing_infrastructure_packages, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

source(file.path(project_root, "R", "modeling_functions.R"))

artifacts <- load_modeling_artifacts(processed_dir)

# Keep only the approved modeling roles. Audit and quality-check fields remain
# in train_prepared for later subgroup analysis, not in this model-development object.
model_data <- artifacts$train[
  c("SK_ID_CURR", "TARGET", artifacts$predictors)
]
model_data <- prepare_model_outcome(model_data)
```

`prepare_model_outcome()` converts the numeric outcome into a labeled factor whose first level is `payment_difficulty`. This makes the event definition explicit and consistent with `yardstick` defaults. It avoids accidentally reporting discrimination for the majority class.

## Stratified three-fold cross-validation

```{r}
#| label: create-validated-folds

cv_folds <- create_stratified_folds(
  model_data,
  outcome_col = "TARGET",
  v = 3L,
  seed = model_seed
)

validate_cv_folds(
  cv_folds,
  id_col = "SK_ID_CURR",
  outcome_col = "TARGET",
  expected_v = 3L
)

fold_summary <- summarize_cv_folds(cv_folds)

knitr::kable(
  fold_summary,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Stratified cross-validation fold sizes and payment-difficulty rates",
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
)
```

Every applicant appears in exactly one assessment fold and never appears in both the analysis and assessment portions of the same fold. Stratification keeps the payment-difficulty rate close to the full training rate in each portion.

The resample object retains the approved predictor columns, but it does not make the globally prepared values safe for model fitting. In the next section, each model workflow must estimate learned preprocessing independently within each analysis fold before it scores the corresponding assessment fold.

## Common evaluation metrics

```{r}
#| label: define-metrics

comparison_metrics <- model_metric_set()

metric_contract <- data.frame(
  metric = c("ROC-AUC", "Accuracy"),
  role = c("Primary model-comparison metric", "Secondary benchmark diagnostic"),
  reason = c(
    "Evaluates ranking across thresholds and is less misleading under imbalance",
    "Required for the simple benchmark but sensitive to the majority class"
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  metric_contract,
  caption = "Metrics used consistently across candidate models"
)
```

The reusable metric set will calculate ROC-AUC and accuracy from the same assessment predictions. Candidate selection will use ROC-AUC; high accuracy alone will not qualify a model as useful.

## Infrastructure tests

The checks below test determinism, fold separation, event ordering, metric summarization, and the guard against comparing candidates evaluated on different folds. Expected errors are captured silently so the rendered notebook remains concise.

```{r}
#| label: test-modeling-infrastructure

cv_folds_repeat <- create_stratified_folds(
  model_data,
  outcome_col = "TARGET",
  v = 3L,
  seed = model_seed
)

assessment_ids <- function(folds) {
  lapply(
    folds$splits,
    function(split) rsample::assessment(split)$SK_ID_CURR
  )
}

example_metrics <- data.frame(
  .metric = rep(c("roc_auc", "accuracy"), each = 3),
  .estimate = c(0.70, 0.71, 0.69, 0.92, 0.91, 0.92)
)
example_summary <- summarize_resample_metrics(example_metrics)

valid_result <- data.frame(id = cv_folds$id)
invalid_result <- data.frame(id = cv_folds$id[-1])

invalid_resample_guard <- inherits(
  try(
    assert_common_resamples(
      list(invalid_candidate = invalid_result),
      expected_ids = cv_folds$id
    ),
    silent = TRUE
  ),
  "try-error"
)

infrastructure_checks <- c(
  "Same seed reproduces assessment membership" = identical(
    assessment_ids(cv_folds),
    assessment_ids(cv_folds_repeat)
  ),
  "Payment difficulty is the event level" = identical(
    levels(model_data$TARGET)[1],
    payment_difficulty_level
  ),
  "Three folds are present" = nrow(cv_folds) == 3L,
  "Metric summary returns both metrics" = setequal(
    example_summary$.metric,
    c("roc_auc", "accuracy")
  ),
  "Matching resample IDs pass" = isTRUE(
    assert_common_resamples(
      list(example_candidate = valid_result),
      expected_ids = cv_folds$id
    )
  ),
  "Mismatched resample IDs are rejected" = invalid_resample_guard
)

if (!all(infrastructure_checks)) {
  stop(
    "Section 2 infrastructure test(s) failed: ",
    paste(names(infrastructure_checks)[!infrastructure_checks], collapse = "; ")
  )
}

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    test = names(infrastructure_checks),
    result = ifelse(infrastructure_checks, "Passed", "Failed")
  ),
  caption = "Reusable modeling infrastructure tests"
)
```

## Section 2 result

Section 2 establishes one reproducible set of stratified 3-fold resamples, an explicit positive outcome, a shared metric definition, and safeguards against incompatible model comparisons. All infrastructure tests must pass before model fitting begins. No benchmark or candidate model has been trained in this section.

**Takeaway from Section 2:** Every candidate will be judged on the same applicants and metric definitions, making the comparisons directly comparable.

# Section 3: Fold-safe feature engineering and preprocessing

**Purpose**

Data preparation created two new modeling-base artifacts at the applicant grain. They contain fixed, decision-time-safe cleaning, application feature engineering, and supplementary aggregation, but they have not undergone any data-learned preprocessing. They are the correct inputs for cross-validation because each analysis fold can learn its own caps, bins, medians, and category levels.

The globally prepared tables from Section 1 remain appropriate for a final model fitted to all training rows. They are not used to estimate cross-validated performance.

## Modeling-base validation

```{r}
#| label: load-modeling-bases

source(file.path(project_root, "R", "modeling_recipes.R"))

base_paths <- file.path(
  processed_dir,
  c("train_modeling_base.rds", "test_modeling_base.rds")
)

if (!all(file.exists(base_paths))) {
  stop(
    "The pre-recipe modeling-base files are missing. Rerun the data-preparation notebook."
  )
}

train_modeling_base <- readRDS(base_paths[1])
test_modeling_base <- readRDS(base_paths[2])

base_checks <- c(
  "Training applicant grain changed" =
    identical(train_modeling_base$SK_ID_CURR, train_prepared$SK_ID_CURR),
  "Test applicant grain changed" =
    identical(test_modeling_base$SK_ID_CURR, test_prepared$SK_ID_CURR),
  "Training target changed" =
    identical(train_modeling_base$TARGET, train_prepared$TARGET),
  "TARGET appears in the scoring base" =
    !"TARGET" %in% names(test_modeling_base),
  "Training base IDs are duplicated" =
    !anyDuplicated(train_modeling_base$SK_ID_CURR),
  "Test base IDs are duplicated" =
    !anyDuplicated(test_modeling_base$SK_ID_CURR)
)

if (!all(base_checks)) {
  stop(
    "Modeling-base validation failed: ",
    paste(names(base_checks)[!base_checks], collapse = "; ")
  )
}

base_summary <- data.frame(
  population = c("Training", "Test"),
  applicants = c(nrow(train_modeling_base), nrow(test_modeling_base)),
  source_columns = c(ncol(train_modeling_base), ncol(test_modeling_base)),
  learned_preprocessing_applied = "No"
)

knitr::kable(
  base_summary,
  caption = "Pre-recipe modeling-base artifacts",
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
)
```

The base tables match the applicant order and outcome created during data preparation. Their transformations are fixed rules: they do not estimate a population median, percentile, bin boundary, or category vocabulary.

## Reproducible feature-set manifests

The application-only feature set provides the controlled comparison required to measure the incremental value of historical data. The full feature set adds bureau, previous-application, installment, POS/CASH, credit-card coverage, unmatched-history, and cross-source coverage fields.

```{r}
#| label: feature-set-manifests

feature_manifests <- build_feature_manifests(train_modeling_base)

manifest_checks <- c(
  "Application manifest is empty" = length(feature_manifests$application) > 0,
  "Supplementary manifest is empty" = length(feature_manifests$supplementary) > 0,
  "Feature sets overlap incorrectly" = length(intersect(
    feature_manifests$application,
    feature_manifests$supplementary
  )) == 0,
  "Full manifest is not the union" = setequal(
    feature_manifests$full,
    c(feature_manifests$application, feature_manifests$supplementary)
  ),
  "ID entered a feature manifest" =
    !"SK_ID_CURR" %in% feature_manifests$full,
  "TARGET entered a feature manifest" =
    !"TARGET" %in% feature_manifests$full,
  "Audit field entered a feature manifest" = !any(
    feature_manifests$audit %in% feature_manifests$full
  )
)

if (!all(manifest_checks)) {
  stop(
    "Feature-manifest validation failed: ",
    paste(names(manifest_checks)[!manifest_checks], collapse = "; ")
  )
}

manifest_summary <- data.frame(
  feature_group = c(
    "Application and engineered application fields",
    "Supplementary history fields",
    "Full candidate set",
    "Audit-only fields",
    "Quality-check fields"
  ),
  source_fields = c(
    length(feature_manifests$application),
    length(feature_manifests$supplementary),
    length(feature_manifests$full),
    length(feature_manifests$audit),
    length(feature_manifests$quality_check)
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  manifest_summary,
  caption = "Pre-recipe fields by approved modeling role"
)
```

These counts refer to source fields before dummy encoding and added capped or log-transformed copies. The final number of model columns is learned independently within each fold.

## Preprocessing design

`build_model_recipe()` returns an untrained recipe for either approved feature set. The recipe preserves the decisions from the EDA and data-preparation phases:

1. The applicant ID, outcome, audit fields, and quality checks receive non-predictor roles.
2. The 1st and 99th percentile caps are learned for the four primary amount fields while the raw values are retained.
3. `log1p` amount features and a separately binned financing-to-goods feature are created.
4. Missingness indicators are created before numeric median imputation for the benchmark and comparison recipes. The selected final XGBoost model replaces this step with native missing-value split routing after the Section 5 ablation.
5. Unseen categories and missing categories receive different levels.
6. Nominal predictors are dummy encoded.
7. Revolving-loan interactions are created for the three affordability ratios.
8. Zero-variance predictors are removed, except reserved `OTHER_UNSEEN` columns.

No class-imbalance sampling is included. Sampling belongs to a later controlled experiment and must occur only within analysis folds.

```{r}
#| label: define-fold-safe-recipes

train_modeling_base <- prepare_model_outcome(train_modeling_base)

application_recipe <- build_model_recipe(
  train_modeling_base,
  feature_set = "application"
)
full_history_recipe <- build_model_recipe(
  train_modeling_base,
  feature_set = "full"
)

recipe_summary <- data.frame(
  recipe = c("Application only", "Application plus supplementary history"),
  source_predictors = c(
    length(feature_manifests$application),
    length(feature_manifests$full)
  ),
  learned_now = "No; parameters are estimated during prep() within a resample"
)

knitr::kable(
  recipe_summary,
  caption = "Reusable untrained preprocessing recipes"
)
```

The recipe definitions can be placed directly in later tidymodels workflows. During resampling, `prep()` is run separately for each analysis fold; the resulting fold recipe is then applied unchanged to its assessment fold.

## Real-fold preprocessing test

The first approved fold provides a full-scale test. Applicant IDs from Section 2 select the same fold membership from the pre-recipe table, ensuring that the modeling data and the resampling plan remain aligned.

```{r}
#| label: test-real-fold-preprocessing

fold_1_analysis_ids <- rsample::analysis(cv_folds$splits[[1]])$SK_ID_CURR
fold_1_assessment_ids <- rsample::assessment(cv_folds$splits[[1]])$SK_ID_CURR

fold_1_analysis <- train_modeling_base[
  match(fold_1_analysis_ids, train_modeling_base$SK_ID_CURR),
]
fold_1_assessment <- train_modeling_base[
  match(fold_1_assessment_ids, train_modeling_base$SK_ID_CURR),
]

if (anyNA(fold_1_analysis$SK_ID_CURR) || anyNA(fold_1_assessment$SK_ID_CURR)) {
  stop("Fold IDs did not align with the modeling-base table.")
}

# Rebuild on the analysis data so this standalone test makes the fitting boundary visible.
fold_1_recipe <- build_model_recipe(fold_1_analysis, feature_set = "full")
fold_1_prepped <- recipes::prep(
  fold_1_recipe,
  training = fold_1_analysis,
  retain = TRUE
)
fold_1_analysis_baked <- recipes::juice(fold_1_prepped)
fold_1_assessment_baked <- recipes::bake(
  fold_1_prepped,
  new_data = fold_1_assessment
)

validate_baked_fold(
  fold_1_prepped,
  fold_1_analysis_baked,
  fold_1_assessment_baked
)

fold_1_roles <- summary(fold_1_prepped)
fold_1_predictors <- fold_1_roles$variable[
  fold_1_roles$role == "predictor"
]

fold_bake_summary <- data.frame(
  population = c("Analysis", "Assessment"),
  applicants = c(nrow(fold_1_analysis_baked), nrow(fold_1_assessment_baked)),
  baked_columns = c(ncol(fold_1_analysis_baked), ncol(fold_1_assessment_baked)),
  predictors = length(fold_1_predictors),
  missing_predictor_values = c(
    sum(is.na(fold_1_analysis_baked[fold_1_predictors])),
    sum(is.na(fold_1_assessment_baked[fold_1_predictors]))
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  fold_bake_summary,
  caption = "Fold 1 preprocessing validation",
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
)
```

Analysis and assessment applicants have identical baked columns, and all model predictors are numeric and complete. The applicant ID and audit fields remain available for alignment and later subgroup review without entering the predictor matrix.

## Evidence that parameters are analysis-fold learned

```{r}
#| label: verify-fold-learned-parameters

fold_caps <- recipes::tidy(fold_1_prepped, id = "cap_amounts")

expected_fold_caps <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  fold_caps$terms,
  function(field) {
    values <- stats::quantile(
      fold_1_analysis[[field]],
      probs = c(0.01, 0.99),
      na.rm = TRUE,
      names = FALSE
    )
    data.frame(
      terms = field,
      expected_lower = values[1],
      expected_upper = values[2]
    )
  }
))

cap_evidence <- merge(fold_caps, expected_fold_caps, by = "terms", sort = FALSE)
cap_matches_analysis <- isTRUE(all.equal(
  cap_evidence$lower_cap,
  cap_evidence$expected_lower,
  tolerance = 1e-10
)) && isTRUE(all.equal(
  cap_evidence$upper_cap,
  cap_evidence$expected_upper,
  tolerance = 1e-10
))

if (!cap_matches_analysis) {
  stop("Stored caps do not match the analysis-fold quantiles.")
}

knitr::kable(
  cap_evidence[
    c("terms", "lower_cap", "upper_cap", "expected_lower", "expected_upper")
  ],
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Stored caps compared with independently calculated Fold 1 analysis quantiles",
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
)
```

The stored values exactly match independent calculations from the analysis fold. The assessment rows were not supplied to `prep()` and therefore could not influence these parameters.

## Novel-category and role tests

```{r}
#| label: test-novel-category-and-roles

novel_case <- fold_1_assessment[1, , drop = FALSE]
novel_case$NAME_INCOME_TYPE <- "SECTION3_TEST_UNSEEN"
novel_case_baked <- recipes::bake(fold_1_prepped, new_data = novel_case)
novel_dummy <- "NAME_INCOME_TYPE_OTHER_UNSEEN"

section_3_checks <- c(
  "Analysis/assessment schemas match" = identical(
    names(fold_1_analysis_baked), names(fold_1_assessment_baked)
  ),
  "Analysis predictors are complete" =
    !anyNA(fold_1_analysis_baked[fold_1_predictors]),
  "Assessment predictors are complete" =
    !anyNA(fold_1_assessment_baked[fold_1_predictors]),
  "Applicant ID is excluded" = !"SK_ID_CURR" %in% fold_1_predictors,
  "Outcome is excluded" = !"TARGET" %in% fold_1_predictors,
  "Audit fields are excluded" = !any(
    feature_manifests$audit %in% fold_1_predictors
  ),
  "Novel-category column is retained" = novel_dummy %in% names(novel_case_baked),
  "Novel category maps explicitly" =
    novel_dummy %in% names(novel_case_baked) && novel_case_baked[[novel_dummy]] == 1,
  "Caps match analysis-fold estimates" = cap_matches_analysis
)

if (!all(section_3_checks)) {
  stop(
    "Section 3 test(s) failed: ",
    paste(names(section_3_checks)[!section_3_checks], collapse = "; ")
  )
}

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    test = names(section_3_checks),
    result = ifelse(section_3_checks, "Passed", "Failed")
  ),
  caption = "Fold-safe preprocessing tests"
)
```

## Section 3 result

Section 3 establishes leak-resistant modeling inputs, two traceable feature sets, and reusable recipes whose learned parameters are estimated within analysis folds. The full-scale Fold 1 test confirms consistent schemas, complete numeric predictors, explicit handling of unseen categories, and exclusion of IDs and governance-audit fields. No model has been fitted.

**Takeaway from Section 3:** The comparisons that follow are leak-resistant, so performance differences reflect the feature sets and models rather than preprocessing learned from assessment rows.

# Section 4: Performance benchmarks

**Purpose**

The first benchmark represents the result of making no meaningful risk distinction: every applicant is assigned to the majority class. Its high accuracy shows the effect of the approximately 8% payment-difficulty rate, while its ROC-AUC establishes the no-discrimination reference of 0.50.

A second benchmark uses a deliberately small application-only logistic regression. It tests whether a conventional, interpretable statistical model can rank risk before supplementary history, complex algorithms, imbalance adjustments, or tuning are introduced.

**Connection:** With the leakage controls established in Sections 1–3, these benchmarks define the minimum performance that every later modeling choice must exceed.

**Method**

## Resample alignment on the modeling base

The Section 2 folds were originally created on the globally prepared table to establish membership. The same seed, applicant order, and stratification are now used on the pre-recipe modeling base. The assertion below requires identical assessment applicants in every fold.

```{r}
#| label: align-modeling-base-folds

# Recreate folds on the pre-recipe table, then prove applicant membership is unchanged.
modeling_cv_folds <- create_stratified_folds(
  train_modeling_base,
  outcome_col = "TARGET",
  v = 3L,
  seed = model_seed
)

validate_cv_folds(
  modeling_cv_folds,
  id_col = "SK_ID_CURR",
  outcome_col = "TARGET",
  expected_v = 3L
)

same_fold_membership <- identical(
  lapply(cv_folds$splits, function(split) {
    rsample::assessment(split)$SK_ID_CURR
  }),
  lapply(modeling_cv_folds$splits, function(split) {
    rsample::assessment(split)$SK_ID_CURR
  })
)

if (!same_fold_membership) {
  stop("Modeling-base folds do not match the approved Section 2 membership.")
}

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    validation = c(
      "Three stratified folds",
      "Same assessment applicants as Section 2",
      "Pre-recipe modeling base used"
    ),
    result = "Passed"
  ),
  caption = "Benchmark resample alignment"
)
```

## Majority-class benchmark

Within each fold, the benchmark assigns every assessment applicant to `no_payment_difficulty`. Its probability estimate for payment difficulty is the prevalence observed in that fold's analysis portion. Because this probability is constant within a fold, the model cannot rank applicants and its ROC-AUC is 0.50.

```{r}
#| label: majority-benchmark

majority_metrics <- evaluate_majority_benchmark(modeling_cv_folds) |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = "Majority class", .before = 1)

knitr::kable(
  majority_metrics[c("model", "id", ".metric", ".estimate")],
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Fold-level majority-class benchmark performance"
)
```

Accuracy remains close to 92% even though the benchmark has no discrimination. This is why candidate models will not be selected on accuracy.

## Simple application-only logistic benchmark

The logistic benchmark uses twelve source predictors chosen from the EDA and industry context:

| Predictor group | Fields | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| External risk scores | `EXT_SOURCE_1`, `EXT_SOURCE_2`, `EXT_SOURCE_3` | Existing application-time risk information; useful for ranking but anonymized and subject to later explainability review |
| Requested financing | Credit, annuity, income, and goods amounts | Loan size and reported repayment capacity |
| Affordability proxies | Annuity-to-income, credit-to-income, and financing-to-goods | EDA-supported measures of financial burden |
| Product | Contract type | The EDA found different risk structures by product |
| Employment stability | Employment duration | A conventional repayment-capacity indicator |

The recipe caps the four amount fields using analysis-fold percentiles, creates missingness indicators for the external scores, imputes numeric fields with analysis-fold medians, and dummy encodes contract type. It excludes historical supplementary tables, audit-only fields, class balancing, and hyperparameter tuning.

```{r}
#| label: simple-logistic-benchmark

benchmark_recipe <- build_simple_logistic_recipe(train_modeling_base)

benchmark_model <- parsnip::logistic_reg() |>
  parsnip::set_engine("glm") |>
  parsnip::set_mode("classification")

benchmark_workflow <- workflows::workflow() |>
  workflows::add_recipe(benchmark_recipe) |>
  workflows::add_model(benchmark_model)

logistic_resamples <- fit_resampled_workflow(
  benchmark_workflow,
  folds = modeling_cv_folds,
  metrics = comparison_metrics,
  seed = model_seed
)

logistic_notes <- tune::collect_notes(logistic_resamples)
if (nrow(logistic_notes) > 0) {
  stop(
    "The simple logistic benchmark produced resampling notes; review before comparison."
  )
}

logistic_metrics <- collect_fold_metrics(
  logistic_resamples,
  model_label = "Simple logistic"
)

knitr::kable(
  logistic_metrics,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Fold-level simple-logistic benchmark performance"
)
```

**Results**

## Benchmark comparison

```{r}
#| label: compare-benchmarks

benchmark_fold_metrics <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  majority_metrics[c("model", "id", ".metric", ".estimate")],
  logistic_metrics
)

assert_common_resamples(
  split(benchmark_fold_metrics, benchmark_fold_metrics$model),
  expected_ids = modeling_cv_folds$id
)

benchmark_comparison <- benchmark_fold_metrics |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$model, .data$.metric) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean = mean(.data$.estimate),
    std_dev = stats::sd(.data$.estimate),
    std_error = stats::sd(.data$.estimate) / sqrt(dplyr::n()),
    folds = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(.data$.metric, .data$model)

majority_auc <- benchmark_comparison$mean[
  benchmark_comparison$model == "Majority class" &
    benchmark_comparison$.metric == "roc_auc"
]
logistic_auc <- benchmark_comparison$mean[
  benchmark_comparison$model == "Simple logistic" &
    benchmark_comparison$.metric == "roc_auc"
]

benchmark_checks <- c(
  "Majority ROC-AUC equals 0.50" = isTRUE(all.equal(majority_auc, 0.5)),
  "Simple logistic beats majority ROC-AUC" = logistic_auc > majority_auc,
  "Both benchmarks use all three folds" = all(
    benchmark_comparison$folds == 3L
  ),
  "Both benchmarks use approved resamples" = isTRUE(
    assert_common_resamples(
      split(benchmark_fold_metrics, benchmark_fold_metrics$model),
      expected_ids = modeling_cv_folds$id
    )
  )
)

if (!all(benchmark_checks)) {
  stop(
    "Benchmark validation failed: ",
    paste(names(benchmark_checks)[!benchmark_checks], collapse = "; ")
  )
}

knitr::kable(
  benchmark_comparison,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Cross-validated benchmark comparison"
)
```

The majority classifier is the formal no-skill benchmark: its high accuracy comes entirely from class imbalance, and its ROC-AUC is 0.50. The simple logistic model provides the more useful modeling benchmark because it must rank applicants using a small application-only feature set. Its improvement in cross-validated ROC-AUC demonstrates that the available application information contains out-of-sample ranking signal.

**Implications**

`r if (logistic_auc > majority_auc) sprintf("The simple logistic benchmark improves ROC-AUC from %.4f to %.4f, so later candidates must beat %.4f to add value beyond basic application information.", majority_auc, logistic_auc, logistic_auc) else "The simple logistic model did not beat the no-skill benchmark, so the application predictors would need to be reconsidered before more complex modeling."` The comparison remains threshold-neutral; no approval cutoff or business lift is inferred.

**Takeaway from Section 4:** `r if (logistic_auc > majority_auc) "The data contain genuine ranking signal, and the simple logistic ROC-AUC is the meaningful benchmark for the candidate-model comparison." else "No reliable ranking signal has yet been demonstrated."`

# Section 5: Candidate model comparison

**Purpose**

This section compares linear and nonlinear candidates using the same three folds, outcome definition, fold-safe preprocessing, and evaluation metrics. Settings are fixed in advance so the results describe broad modeling ideas rather than a hyperparameter search.

The comparison separates two questions:

1. Does the approved supplementary history improve a regularized logistic model beyond application information alone?
2. Do nonlinear tree ensembles improve ranking beyond the linear candidates?

No candidate uses class weighting, upsampling, downsampling, SMOTE, or tuned parameters in this section.

**Connection:** The benchmark from Section 4 becomes the reference for testing whether richer features and nonlinear algorithms add out-of-sample ranking value.

**Method**

## Candidate specifications

```{r}
#| label: define-candidate-models

candidate_packages <- c("glmnet", "ranger", "xgboost")
missing_candidate_packages <- candidate_packages[
  !vapply(candidate_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]
if (length(missing_candidate_packages)) {
  stop(
    "Install the following candidate-model package(s): ",
    paste(missing_candidate_packages, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

ridge_spec <- parsnip::logistic_reg(
  penalty = 0.001,
  mixture = 0
) |>
  parsnip::set_engine("glmnet") |>
  parsnip::set_mode("classification")

forest_spec <- parsnip::rand_forest(
  mtry = 14,
  trees = 300,
  min_n = 10
) |>
  parsnip::set_engine(
    "ranger",
    probability = TRUE,
    num.threads = resample_engine_threads,
    seed = model_seed
  ) |>
  parsnip::set_mode("classification")

xgboost_spec <- parsnip::boost_tree(
  mtry = 100,
  trees = 300,
  min_n = 10,
  tree_depth = 6,
  learn_rate = 0.05,
  loss_reduction = 0,
  sample_size = 0.8
) |>
  parsnip::set_engine(
    "xgboost",
    nthread = resample_engine_threads,
    verbosity = 0
  ) |>
  parsnip::set_mode("classification")

candidate_settings <- data.frame(
  candidate = c(
    "Ridge logistic — application",
    "Ridge logistic — full history",
    "XGBoost — application",
    "Random forest — full history",
    "XGBoost — full history"
  ),
  feature_set = c("Application", "Full", "Application", "Full", "Full"),
  fixed_settings = c(
    "penalty = 0.001; mixture = 0",
    "penalty = 0.001; mixture = 0",
    paste(
      "mtry = 100; trees = 300; depth = 6; learn rate = 0.05;",
      "min_n = 10; row sample = 0.8"
    ),
    "mtry = 14; trees = 300; min_n = 10",
    paste(
      "mtry = 100; trees = 300; depth = 6; learn rate = 0.05;",
      "min_n = 10; row sample = 0.8"
    )
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  candidate_settings,
  caption = "Untuned candidate-model specifications"
)
```

The ridge models use the same fixed penalty so the feature-set comparison is controlled. The random forest and XGBoost settings are computationally moderate starting points, not claimed optima. Their purpose is to test whether nonlinear splits and interactions are promising enough to justify later tuning.

## Three-fold candidate evaluation

```{r}
#| label: fit-candidate-models

candidate_spec_signature <- digest::digest(list(
  seed = model_seed,
  ridge = ridge_spec,
  forest = forest_spec,
  xgboost = xgboost_spec,
  application_features = feature_manifests$application,
  full_features = feature_manifests$full,
  fold_ids = modeling_cv_folds$id
))

# The object hash prevents stale reuse when a model specification or feature set changes.
candidate_runs <- cached_modeling_result("candidate_runs", list(
  run_candidate_model(
    model_label = "Ridge logistic — application",
    model_spec = ridge_spec,
    recipe = application_recipe,
    folds = modeling_cv_folds,
    metrics = comparison_metrics,
    seed = model_seed
  ),
  run_candidate_model(
    model_label = "Ridge logistic — full history",
    model_spec = ridge_spec,
    recipe = full_history_recipe,
    folds = modeling_cv_folds,
    metrics = comparison_metrics,
    seed = model_seed
  ),
  run_candidate_model(
    model_label = "XGBoost — application",
    model_spec = xgboost_spec,
    recipe = application_recipe,
    folds = modeling_cv_folds,
    metrics = comparison_metrics,
    seed = model_seed
  ),
  run_candidate_model(
    model_label = "Random forest — full history",
    model_spec = forest_spec,
    recipe = full_history_recipe,
    folds = modeling_cv_folds,
    metrics = comparison_metrics,
    seed = model_seed
  ),
  run_candidate_model(
    model_label = "XGBoost — full history",
    model_spec = xgboost_spec,
    recipe = full_history_recipe,
    folds = modeling_cv_folds,
    metrics = comparison_metrics,
    seed = model_seed,
    retain_predictions = TRUE
  )
), spec_signature = candidate_spec_signature)

candidate_outputs <- combine_candidate_runs(candidate_runs)
candidate_fold_metrics <- candidate_outputs$fold_metrics
candidate_runtime <- candidate_outputs$runtime

assert_common_resamples(
  split(candidate_fold_metrics, candidate_fold_metrics$model),
  expected_ids = modeling_cv_folds$id
)
```

Each workflow refits its recipe inside each analysis fold. The assessment fold is used only after preprocessing and model fitting are complete. Resamples run sequentially by default with four engine threads per XGBoost or ranger fit. If `MODELING_WORKERS` enables parallel folds, each fit uses one engine thread to avoid nested oversubscription.

**Results**

## Fold-level results

```{r}
#| label: candidate-fold-results

candidate_auc_by_fold <- candidate_fold_metrics |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$.metric == "roc_auc") |>
  dplyr::arrange(.data$model, .data$id)

knitr::kable(
  candidate_auc_by_fold,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Candidate ROC-AUC by assessment fold"
)

candidate_notes <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(candidate_runs, function(run) {
  if (!nrow(run$notes)) return(NULL)
  data.frame(model = run$model, run$notes, check.names = FALSE)
}))

if (nrow(candidate_notes)) {
  knitr::kable(
    candidate_notes,
    caption = "Non-error engine notes produced during candidate fitting"
  )
}
```

Fold-level results are retained so a candidate is not selected from an average that hides an unstable assessment fold. Any fitting error would have stopped this section before comparison.

## Cross-validated comparison

```{r}
#| label: compare-candidate-models

all_model_metrics <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  benchmark_fold_metrics,
  candidate_fold_metrics
)

model_comparison <- all_model_metrics |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$model, .data$.metric) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean = mean(.data$.estimate),
    std_dev = stats::sd(.data$.estimate),
    std_error = stats::sd(.data$.estimate) / sqrt(dplyr::n()),
    folds = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(.data$.metric, dplyr::desc(.data$mean))

auc_comparison <- model_comparison |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$.metric == "roc_auc") |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(.data$mean))

knitr::kable(
  auc_comparison,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Cross-validated ROC-AUC comparison"
)

knitr::kable(
  candidate_runtime,
  digits = 1,
  caption = "Elapsed time for three-fold candidate evaluation"
)
```

Runtime is reported as an operational consideration, not a performance metric. It depends on the available computer and should be interpreted comparatively within this run.

## Supplementary-data and algorithm findings

```{r}
#| label: candidate-findings

auc_lookup <- stats::setNames(auc_comparison$mean, auc_comparison$model)

supplementary_auc_change <- unname(
  auc_lookup["Ridge logistic — full history"] -
    auc_lookup["Ridge logistic — application"]
)
xgboost_supplementary_auc_change <- unname(
  auc_lookup["XGBoost — full history"] -
    auc_lookup["XGBoost — application"]
)
best_candidate <- candidate_auc_by_fold |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$model) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mean_auc = mean(.data$.estimate), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(.data$mean_auc)) |>
  dplyr::slice(1)

candidate_checks <- c(
  "Every candidate has three ROC-AUC estimates" = all(
    table(candidate_auc_by_fold$model) == 3L
  ),
  "Every candidate beats the majority benchmark" = all(
    candidate_auc_by_fold |>
      dplyr::group_by(.data$model) |>
      dplyr::summarise(mean_auc = mean(.data$.estimate), .groups = "drop") |>
      dplyr::pull(.data$mean_auc) > majority_auc
  ),
  "At least one candidate beats the simple logistic benchmark" =
    best_candidate$mean_auc > logistic_auc,
  "No candidate fit produced an error note" = all(vapply(
    candidate_runs,
    function(run) !nrow(run$notes) || !any(run$notes$type == "error"),
    logical(1)
  ))
)

if (!all(candidate_checks)) {
  stop(
    "Candidate comparison validation failed: ",
    paste(names(candidate_checks)[!candidate_checks], collapse = "; ")
  )
}

finding_summary <- data.frame(
  question = c(
    "Change from supplementary history in ridge logistic",
    "Change from supplementary history in XGBoost",
    "Best untuned candidate",
    "Best untuned mean ROC-AUC",
    "Project target reached"
  ),
  result = c(
    sprintf("%+.4f ROC-AUC", supplementary_auc_change),
    sprintf("%+.4f ROC-AUC", xgboost_supplementary_auc_change),
    best_candidate$model,
    sprintf("%.4f", best_candidate$mean_auc),
    ifelse(best_candidate$mean_auc >= 0.79, "Yes", "No")
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  finding_summary,
  caption = "Candidate-model findings"
)
```

The controlled ridge and XGBoost comparisons estimate the incremental value of supplementary history under the same algorithm settings. The remaining tree comparison shows whether a different nonlinear ensemble adds value. These are predictive associations, not causal effects or evidence that every included field is suitable for a final lending policy.

Random forest was evaluated only with the full-history feature set. `r if (unname(auc_lookup["Random forest — full history"]) < max(unname(auc_lookup[c("Ridge logistic — full history", "XGBoost — full history")]))) "Because full-history random forest already trailed the stronger full-history ridge and XGBoost candidates, an additional application-only forest run was not prioritized." else "Because full-history random forest remained competitive, an application-only forest comparison should be considered in a later expansion."`

## Missing-data handling experiment

The primary recipe adds missingness indicators for heavily missing credit-risk fields and imputes numeric predictors with analysis-fold medians. XGBoost can instead retain numeric missing values and learn a default branch direction at each split. The experiment below removes only the missing-indicator and median-imputation steps, then compares both approaches using the same full-history XGBoost specification and assessment folds.

```{r}
#| label: compare-xgboost-missing-strategies

# Clone the validated recipe, then remove only the two explicit numeric-missing steps.
native_missing_recipe <- full_history_recipe
native_missing_recipe$steps <- Filter(
  function(step) {
    !inherits(step, "step_indicate_na") &&
      !inherits(step, "step_impute_median")
  },
  native_missing_recipe$steps
)

removed_missing_steps <- setdiff(
  vapply(full_history_recipe$steps, function(step) class(step)[1], character(1)),
  vapply(native_missing_recipe$steps, function(step) class(step)[1], character(1))
)
stopifnot(
  "Native-missing recipe must remove the indicator and median-imputation steps" =
    setequal(removed_missing_steps, c("step_indicate_na", "step_impute_median"))
)

missing_strategy_signature <- digest::digest(list(
  seed = model_seed,
  model = xgboost_spec,
  retain_predictions = TRUE,
  removed_steps = sort(removed_missing_steps),
  features = feature_manifests$full,
  fold_ids = modeling_cv_folds$id
))

# Cache this additional three-fold experiment independently from the main candidates.
native_missing_run <- cached_modeling_result(
  "xgboost_native_missing",
  run_candidate_model(
    model_label = "XGBoost — full history, native missing",
    model_spec = xgboost_spec,
    recipe = native_missing_recipe,
    folds = modeling_cv_folds,
    metrics = comparison_metrics,
    seed = model_seed,
    retain_predictions = TRUE
  ),
  spec_signature = missing_strategy_signature
)

native_missing_summary <- native_missing_run$metrics |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$.metric) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean = mean(.data$.estimate),
    std_error = stats::sd(.data$.estimate) / sqrt(dplyr::n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
native_missing_auc <- native_missing_summary$mean[
  native_missing_summary$.metric == "roc_auc"
]
native_missing_auc_se <- native_missing_summary$std_error[
  native_missing_summary$.metric == "roc_auc"
]
imputed_xgboost_auc <- unname(auc_lookup["XGBoost — full history"])
missing_strategy_change <- native_missing_auc - imputed_xgboost_auc

missing_strategy_comparison <- data.frame(
  strategy = c(
    "Median imputation plus missingness indicators",
    "Native XGBoost missing-value routing"
  ),
  mean_roc_auc = c(imputed_xgboost_auc, native_missing_auc),
  std_error = c(
    auc_comparison$std_error[
      auc_comparison$model == "XGBoost — full history"
    ],
    native_missing_auc_se
  ),
  elapsed_seconds = c(
    candidate_runtime$elapsed_seconds[
      candidate_runtime$model == "XGBoost — full history"
    ],
    native_missing_run$elapsed_seconds
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  missing_strategy_comparison,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Full-history XGBoost missing-data experiment"
)
```

`r if (missing_strategy_change > 0) sprintf("Native missing-value routing improves mean ROC-AUC by %+.4f and should be considered for final selection.", missing_strategy_change) else sprintf("Median imputation plus missingness indicators remains stronger by %.4f ROC-AUC, so the established recipe is retained.", abs(missing_strategy_change))`

**Implications**

`r if (best_candidate$mean_auc > logistic_auc) sprintf("The best untuned candidate, %s, improves mean ROC-AUC from %.4f to %.4f; supplementary history changes XGBoost ROC-AUC by %+.4f.", best_candidate$model, logistic_auc, best_candidate$mean_auc, xgboost_supplementary_auc_change) else sprintf("No untuned candidate improves on the simple logistic ROC-AUC of %.4f.", logistic_auc)` The result narrows the candidates for imbalance testing but does not establish an approval threshold.

**Takeaway from Section 5:** `r if (native_missing_auc > imputed_xgboost_auc) "Native-missing full-history XGBoost is the strongest untuned modeling direction." else if (identical(best_candidate$model, "XGBoost — full history")) "Imputed full-history XGBoost is the strongest untuned modeling direction." else sprintf("%s is the strongest untuned modeling direction.", best_candidate$model)` The imbalance and tuning experiments below retain the median-imputation recipe as their common controlled baseline; the native-missing alternative is carried separately to final selection in Section 9.

# Section 6: Class-imbalance strategies

**Purpose**

Only about 8% of training applicants experienced payment difficulty. Section 5 used the observed distribution without adjustment. This section holds the median-imputation full-history XGBoost baseline fixed and changes only how the analysis-fold classes influence fitting. The imbalance and later tuning experiments were not repeated with native missing-value routing; that alternative remains eligible and is carried directly to final selection in Section 9.

Four strategies are compared:

1. **Unadjusted:** retain the observed analysis-fold distribution.
2. **Class weighted:** retain every row but increase the XGBoost loss weight for the event class by 11.4, the approximate negative-to-positive ratio implied by the EDA baseline.
3. **Downsampled:** randomly retain equal counts of majority and minority analysis rows.
4. **SMOTE:** create synthetic minority rows until the minority count is half the majority count.

Sampling is never applied to assessment folds. The model specification and assessment applicants remain unchanged, so differences are attributable to the imbalance strategy rather than tuning or a different validation sample.

**Connection:** The strongest untuned Section 5 model is held fixed here so only the treatment of class imbalance changes.

**Method**

## Sampling recipes

```{r}
#| label: define-imbalance-recipes

if (!requireNamespace("themis", quietly = TRUE)) {
  stop("Install package 'themis' before running the imbalance experiments.")
}

downsample_recipe <- add_imbalance_strategy(
  full_history_recipe,
  strategy = "downsample",
  seed = model_seed,
  under_ratio = 1
)

smote_recipe <- add_imbalance_strategy(
  full_history_recipe,
  strategy = "smote",
  seed = model_seed,
  over_ratio = 0.5
)

imbalance_design <- data.frame(
  strategy = c("Unadjusted", "Class weighted", "Downsampled", "SMOTE"),
  analysis_fold_change = c(
    "None",
    "Event loss weight = 11.4; all rows retained",
    "Majority randomly reduced to the minority count",
    "Synthetic minority rows added to minority/majority = 0.5"
  ),
  assessment_fold_change = "None"
)

knitr::kable(
  imbalance_design,
  caption = "Controlled class-imbalance experiment"
)
```

The 11.4 weight is declared from the approximately 8% project baseline rather than recalculated from assessment outcomes. Sampling steps use `skip = TRUE`, the recipes convention that applies them while preparing analysis data but skips them when new assessment or scoring data are baked.

## Sampling-boundary test

```{r}
#| label: test-sampling-boundary

sampling_test_recipes <- list(
  Downsampled = build_model_recipe(fold_1_analysis, feature_set = "full") |>
    add_imbalance_strategy(
      strategy = "downsample",
      seed = model_seed,
      under_ratio = 1
    ),
  SMOTE = build_model_recipe(fold_1_analysis, feature_set = "full") |>
    add_imbalance_strategy(
      strategy = "smote",
      seed = model_seed,
      over_ratio = 0.5
    )
)

sampling_test_results <- lapply(names(sampling_test_recipes), function(strategy) {
  trained <- recipes::prep(
    sampling_test_recipes[[strategy]],
    training = fold_1_analysis,
    retain = TRUE
  )
  sampled_analysis <- recipes::juice(trained)
  untouched_assessment <- recipes::bake(trained, new_data = fold_1_assessment)

  analysis_counts <- table(sampled_analysis$TARGET)
  assessment_counts <- table(untouched_assessment$TARGET)

  data.frame(
    strategy = strategy,
    original_analysis_rows = nrow(fold_1_analysis),
    sampled_analysis_rows = nrow(sampled_analysis),
    sampled_events = unname(analysis_counts[payment_difficulty_level]),
    sampled_non_events = unname(analysis_counts[no_payment_difficulty_level]),
    assessment_rows_before = nrow(fold_1_assessment),
    assessment_rows_after = nrow(untouched_assessment),
    assessment_distribution_unchanged = identical(
      table(fold_1_assessment$TARGET),
      assessment_counts
    )
  )
})

sampling_test_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(sampling_test_results)

if (!all(
  sampling_test_summary$assessment_rows_before ==
    sampling_test_summary$assessment_rows_after &
    sampling_test_summary$assessment_distribution_unchanged
)) {
  stop("A sampling strategy changed the assessment fold.")
}

knitr::kable(
  sampling_test_summary,
  caption = "Fold 1 sampling and assessment-boundary validation",
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
)
```

This executed test proves that sampling changes only the analysis data supplied to the model. The natural event rate and applicant count are preserved in assessment, so performance is measured on the original population distribution.

## Adjusted XGBoost specifications

```{r}
#| label: define-imbalance-models

weighted_xgboost_spec <- parsnip::boost_tree(
  mtry = 100,
  trees = 300,
  min_n = 10,
  tree_depth = 6,
  learn_rate = 0.05,
  loss_reduction = 0,
  sample_size = 0.8
) |>
  parsnip::set_engine(
    "xgboost",
    nthread = resample_engine_threads,
    verbosity = 0,
    scale_pos_weight = 11.4
  ) |>
  parsnip::set_mode("classification")

imbalance_specs <- data.frame(
  strategy = c("Class weighted", "Downsampled", "SMOTE"),
  model = "Same 300-tree XGBoost structure as Section 5",
  changed_component = c(
    "scale_pos_weight = 11.4",
    "analysis-fold recipe only",
    "analysis-fold recipe only"
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  imbalance_specs,
  caption = "Adjusted candidates relative to unadjusted XGBoost"
)
```

## Three-fold imbalance comparison

```{r}
#| label: fit-imbalance-strategies

downsample_step <- Filter(
  function(step) inherits(step, "step_downsample"),
  downsample_recipe$steps
)[[1]]
smote_step <- Filter(
  function(step) inherits(step, "step_smote"),
  smote_recipe$steps
)[[1]]
imbalance_spec_signature <- digest::digest(list(
  seed = model_seed,
  unadjusted = xgboost_spec,
  weighted = weighted_xgboost_spec,
  downsample = downsample_step[c(
    "under_ratio", "ratio", "replacement", "skip", "seed"
  )],
  smote = smote_step[c(
    "over_ratio", "neighbors", "distance", "indicator_column", "skip", "seed"
  )],
  fold_ids = modeling_cv_folds$id
))

# Each sampling strategy is fitted on the same folds; sampling occurs inside recipes.
imbalance_runs <- cached_modeling_result("imbalance_runs", list(
  run_candidate_model(
    model_label = "XGBoost — class weighted",
    model_spec = weighted_xgboost_spec,
    recipe = full_history_recipe,
    folds = modeling_cv_folds,
    metrics = comparison_metrics,
    seed = model_seed
  ),
  run_candidate_model(
    model_label = "XGBoost — downsampled",
    model_spec = xgboost_spec,
    recipe = downsample_recipe,
    folds = modeling_cv_folds,
    metrics = comparison_metrics,
    seed = model_seed
  ),
  run_candidate_model(
    model_label = "XGBoost — SMOTE",
    model_spec = xgboost_spec,
    recipe = smote_recipe,
    folds = modeling_cv_folds,
    metrics = comparison_metrics,
    seed = model_seed
  )
), spec_signature = imbalance_spec_signature)

imbalance_outputs <- combine_candidate_runs(imbalance_runs)
adjusted_imbalance_metrics <- imbalance_outputs$fold_metrics
adjusted_imbalance_runtime <- imbalance_outputs$runtime

unadjusted_xgboost_metrics <- candidate_fold_metrics |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$model == "XGBoost — full history") |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = "XGBoost — unadjusted")

imbalance_fold_metrics <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  unadjusted_xgboost_metrics,
  adjusted_imbalance_metrics
)

assert_common_resamples(
  split(imbalance_fold_metrics, imbalance_fold_metrics$model),
  expected_ids = modeling_cv_folds$id
)
```

**Results**

## Performance and runtime

```{r}
#| label: compare-imbalance-strategies

imbalance_comparison <- imbalance_fold_metrics |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$model, .data$.metric) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean = mean(.data$.estimate),
    std_dev = stats::sd(.data$.estimate),
    std_error = stats::sd(.data$.estimate) / sqrt(dplyr::n()),
    folds = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(.data$.metric, dplyr::desc(.data$mean))

knitr::kable(
  imbalance_comparison,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Cross-validated class-imbalance comparison"
)

unadjusted_runtime <- candidate_runtime |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$model == "XGBoost — full history") |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = "XGBoost — unadjusted")

imbalance_runtime <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  unadjusted_runtime,
  adjusted_imbalance_runtime
)

knitr::kable(
  imbalance_runtime,
  digits = 1,
  caption = "Elapsed time for three-fold imbalance strategies"
)
```

Accuracy remains secondary. Weighting or sampling can change how many applicants cross the default 0.5 classification threshold, but that threshold has not been tied to approval policy or asymmetric business costs. ROC-AUC remains the appropriate selection measure for this experiment.

## Imbalance finding

```{r}
#| label: imbalance-finding

imbalance_auc <- imbalance_comparison |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$.metric == "roc_auc") |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(.data$mean))

best_imbalance_strategy <- imbalance_auc |>
  dplyr::slice(1)

stopifnot(
  "The Section 7 narrative requires unadjusted XGBoost to win Section 6" =
    identical(best_imbalance_strategy$model, "XGBoost — unadjusted")
)

unadjusted_imbalance_auc <- imbalance_auc$mean[
  imbalance_auc$model == "XGBoost — unadjusted"
]

imbalance_checks <- c(
  "Every strategy has three ROC-AUC estimates" = all(
    table(
      imbalance_fold_metrics$model[
        imbalance_fold_metrics$.metric == "roc_auc"
      ]
    ) == 3L
  ),
  "Every strategy uses approved folds" = isTRUE(
    assert_common_resamples(
      split(imbalance_fold_metrics, imbalance_fold_metrics$model),
      expected_ids = modeling_cv_folds$id
    )
  ),
  "No adjusted fit produced an error" = all(vapply(
    imbalance_runs,
    function(run) !nrow(run$notes) || !any(run$notes$type == "error"),
    logical(1)
  ))
)

if (!all(imbalance_checks)) {
  stop(
    "Imbalance comparison validation failed: ",
    paste(names(imbalance_checks)[!imbalance_checks], collapse = "; ")
  )
}

imbalance_finding <- data.frame(
  finding = c(
    "Best imbalance strategy",
    "Best mean ROC-AUC",
    "Change from unadjusted XGBoost"
  ),
  result = c(
    best_imbalance_strategy$model,
    sprintf("%.4f", best_imbalance_strategy$mean),
    sprintf(
      "%+.4f ROC-AUC",
      best_imbalance_strategy$mean - unadjusted_imbalance_auc
    )
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  imbalance_finding,
  caption = "Class-imbalance experiment finding"
)
```

Weighting and resampling change the training objective and, for SMOTE and downsampling, the apparent analysis-fold class distribution. Their raw predicted probabilities should therefore not automatically be interpreted as calibrated payment-difficulty probabilities. Any adjusted strategy retained after tuning would require calibration assessment on untouched validation predictions.

**Implications**

`r if (identical(best_imbalance_strategy$model, "XGBoost — unadjusted")) sprintf("No tested imbalance adjustment beats unadjusted XGBoost (best mean ROC-AUC %.4f), so tuning should retain the observed class distribution.", best_imbalance_strategy$mean) else sprintf("%s improves mean ROC-AUC by %+.4f and should be carried into tuning.", best_imbalance_strategy$model, best_imbalance_strategy$mean - unadjusted_imbalance_auc)` This conclusion concerns ranking performance, not a decision threshold or subgroup equity.

**Takeaway from Section 6:** `r if (identical(best_imbalance_strategy$model, "XGBoost — unadjusted")) "Class imbalance does not require synthetic sampling or weighting for the selected ranking objective." else "The best-performing imbalance adjustment should accompany the model into tuning."`

# Section 7: Randomized XGBoost tuning

**Purpose**

`r if (identical(best_candidate$model, "XGBoost — full history") && identical(best_imbalance_strategy$model, "XGBoost — unadjusted")) "Unadjusted full-history XGBoost was the strongest candidate across Sections 5 and 6." else sprintf("The strongest Section 5 candidate was %s, and the strongest Section 6 strategy was %s.", best_candidate$model, best_imbalance_strategy$model)` This section searches a broader set of XGBoost configurations using a relatively small stratified sample, 3-fold cross-validation, and 20 randomized space-filling combinations. This follows the assignment's computational guidance and avoids an exhaustive grid.

The tuning-sample results are compared with the untuned XGBoost specification on the **same sample and folds**. They are not treated as directly comparable to the earlier full-data cross-validation estimate.

**Connection:** Section 6 determines the imbalance treatment carried into this search; this section changes model parameters while preserving that choice.

**Method**

## Stratified tuning sample

```{r}
#| label: create-tuning-sample

tuning_sample <- create_tuning_sample(
  train_modeling_base,
  size = 5000L,
  outcome_col = "TARGET",
  seed = model_seed
)

tuning_folds <- create_stratified_folds(
  tuning_sample,
  outcome_col = "TARGET",
  v = 3L,
  seed = model_seed
)

validate_cv_folds(
  tuning_folds,
  id_col = "SK_ID_CURR",
  outcome_col = "TARGET",
  expected_v = 3L
)

full_event_rate <- mean(
  train_modeling_base$TARGET == payment_difficulty_level
)
tuning_event_rate <- mean(
  tuning_sample$TARGET == payment_difficulty_level
)

tuning_sample_checks <- c(
  "Tuning sample is not approximately 5,000 rows" =
    abs(nrow(tuning_sample) - 5000L) <= 10L,
  "Tuning sample IDs are duplicated" =
    !anyDuplicated(tuning_sample$SK_ID_CURR),
  "Tuning prevalence differs materially from full training" =
    abs(tuning_event_rate - full_event_rate) < 0.005,
  "Tuning folds are not three-fold" = nrow(tuning_folds) == 3L
)

if (!all(tuning_sample_checks)) {
  stop(
    "Tuning-sample validation failed: ",
    paste(names(tuning_sample_checks)[!tuning_sample_checks], collapse = "; ")
  )
}

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    population = c("Full training", "Tuning sample"),
    applicants = c(nrow(train_modeling_base), nrow(tuning_sample)),
    payment_difficulty_cases = c(
      sum(train_modeling_base$TARGET == payment_difficulty_level),
      sum(tuning_sample$TARGET == payment_difficulty_level)
    ),
    payment_difficulty_rate = c(full_event_rate, tuning_event_rate)
  ),
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Full training and stratified tuning-sample distributions",
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
)
```

The tuning sample is used only to compare hyperparameters efficiently. The final selected specification will later be fitted using all available training applicants.

## Randomized parameter space

```{r}
#| label: define-randomized-search

tuning_recipe <- build_model_recipe(tuning_sample, feature_set = "full")

tunable_xgboost_spec <- parsnip::boost_tree(
  mtry = tune::tune(),
  trees = tune::tune(),
  min_n = tune::tune(),
  tree_depth = tune::tune(),
  learn_rate = tune::tune(),
  loss_reduction = tune::tune(),
  sample_size = tune::tune()
) |>
  parsnip::set_engine(
    "xgboost",
    nthread = resample_engine_threads,
    verbosity = 0
  ) |>
  parsnip::set_mode("classification")

tuning_workflow <- workflows::workflow() |>
  workflows::add_recipe(tuning_recipe) |>
  workflows::add_model(tunable_xgboost_spec)

tuning_parameters <- hardhat::extract_parameter_set_dials(tuning_workflow) |>
  stats::update(
    mtry = dials::mtry(c(20L, 180L)),
    trees = dials::trees(c(200L, 800L)),
    min_n = dials::min_n(c(5L, 50L)),
    tree_depth = dials::tree_depth(c(2L, 8L)),
    learn_rate = dials::learn_rate(c(-2, log10(0.20))),
    loss_reduction = dials::loss_reduction(c(-3, 1)),
    sample_size = dials::sample_prop(c(0.60, 1.00))
  )

set.seed(model_seed)
tuning_grid <- dials::grid_space_filling(
  tuning_parameters,
  size = 20,
  type = "latin_hypercube"
)

if (nrow(tuning_grid) != 20L || anyDuplicated(tuning_grid)) {
  stop("The randomized search grid must contain 20 unique configurations.")
}

parameter_ranges <- data.frame(
  parameter = c(
    "Predictors per split", "Trees", "Minimum node size", "Tree depth",
    "Learning rate", "Minimum loss reduction", "Row sample"
  ),
  search_range = c(
    "20–180", "200–800", "5–50", "2–8", "0.01–0.20",
    "0.001–10 (log scale)", "0.60–1.00"
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  parameter_ranges,
  caption = "Randomized XGBoost search space"
)
```

The Latin-hypercube design is randomized but spreads 20 candidates across the multidimensional range more efficiently than drawing every parameter independently. It remains a randomized search, not an exhaustive enumeration.

## Execute the 20-candidate search

```{r}
#| label: run-randomized-tuning

tuning_spec_signature <- digest::digest(list(
  seed = model_seed,
  model = tunable_xgboost_spec,
  parameter_ranges = tuning_parameters,
  grid = tuning_grid,
  fold_ids = tuning_folds$id
))

# Evaluate the 20 space-filling configurations across the three tuning folds.
tuning_run <- cached_modeling_result("randomized_tuning", run_randomized_tuning(
  workflow = tuning_workflow,
  folds = tuning_folds,
  grid = tuning_grid,
  metrics = comparison_metrics,
  seed = model_seed,
  selection_metric = "roc_auc"
), spec_signature = tuning_spec_signature)

tuning_auc_folds <- tuning_run$fold_metrics |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$.metric == "roc_auc")

tuning_config_counts <- table(tuning_auc_folds$.config)
if (
  length(tuning_config_counts) != 20L ||
    !all(tuning_config_counts == 3L)
) {
  stop("Each of the 20 tuning configurations must have three ROC-AUC estimates.")
}

if (nrow(tuning_run$notes) > 0) {
  tuning_note_summary <- tuning_run$notes |>
    dplyr::count(.data$type, .data$note, name = "occurrences")
  knitr::kable(
    tuning_note_summary,
    caption = "Compact summary of non-error tuning notes"
  )
}
```

All configurations use the same tuning applicants and fold assignments. Preprocessing is refitted separately inside each fold, just as it was during the full-data candidate comparison.

**Results**

## Leading tuning configurations

```{r}
#| label: rank-tuning-configurations

tuning_accuracy <- tuning_run$summary_metrics |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$.metric == "accuracy") |>
  dplyr::select(.data$.config, accuracy_mean = .data$mean)

tuning_ranked <- tuning_run$summary_metrics |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$.metric == "roc_auc") |>
  dplyr::left_join(tuning_accuracy, by = ".config") |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(.data$mean))

top_tuning_results <- tuning_ranked |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 10) |>
  dplyr::select(
    .data$.config,
    .data$mtry,
    .data$trees,
    .data$min_n,
    .data$tree_depth,
    .data$learn_rate,
    .data$loss_reduction,
    .data$sample_size,
    roc_auc_mean = .data$mean,
    roc_auc_std_error = .data$std_err,
    .data$accuracy_mean
  )

knitr::kable(
  top_tuning_results,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Top randomized configurations ranked by tuning-sample ROC-AUC"
)

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    measurement = c("Configurations", "Folds per configuration", "Elapsed seconds"),
    value = c(20, 3, round(tuning_run$elapsed_seconds, 1))
  ),
  caption = "Randomized-search execution summary"
)
```

The leading configuration is selected on mean ROC-AUC only. Accuracy is displayed for context but does not determine the winner.

## Same-fold untuned control

```{r}
#| label: tuning-sample-control

control_spec_signature <- digest::digest(list(
  seed = model_seed,
  model = xgboost_spec,
  features = feature_manifests$full,
  fold_ids = tuning_folds$id
))

untuned_control <- cached_modeling_result("tuning_sample_control", run_candidate_model(
  model_label = "Untuned XGBoost — tuning sample",
  model_spec = xgboost_spec,
  recipe = tuning_recipe,
  folds = tuning_folds,
  metrics = comparison_metrics,
  seed = model_seed
), spec_signature = control_spec_signature)

untuned_control_summary <- untuned_control$metrics |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$.metric) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean = mean(.data$.estimate),
    std_error = stats::sd(.data$.estimate) / sqrt(dplyr::n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

best_tuning_auc <- tuning_ranked$mean[1]
best_tuning_se <- tuning_ranked$std_err[1]
untuned_tuning_auc <- untuned_control_summary$mean[
  untuned_control_summary$.metric == "roc_auc"
]

same_fold_comparison <- data.frame(
  model = c(
    "Untuned XGBoost — tuning sample",
    "Best randomized configuration — tuning sample"
  ),
  mean_roc_auc = c(untuned_tuning_auc, best_tuning_auc),
  std_error = c(
    untuned_control_summary$std_error[
      untuned_control_summary$.metric == "roc_auc"
    ],
    best_tuning_se
  ),
  folds = 3L
)

knitr::kable(
  same_fold_comparison,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Tuned and untuned XGBoost on identical 5K-sample folds"
)
```

This is the valid estimate of tuning improvement because both rows use identical data and fold assignments. The tuning-sample AUC should not be subtracted from the earlier full-data AUC; sample size and assessment applicants differ.

## Selected parameters

```{r}
#| label: select-tuned-parameters

selected_parameters <- tuning_run$best_parameters

selected_checks <- c(
  "Best configuration is missing" = nrow(selected_parameters) == 1L,
  "Selected configuration lacks a tuning result" =
    selected_parameters$.config %in% tuning_ranked$.config,
  "Tuning produced an error note" =
    !nrow(tuning_run$notes) || !any(tuning_run$notes$type == "error")
)

if (!all(selected_checks)) {
  stop(
    "Tuning selection validation failed: ",
    paste(names(selected_checks)[!selected_checks], collapse = "; ")
  )
}

selected_display <- data.frame(
  parameter = c(
    "mtry", "trees", "min_n", "tree_depth", "learn_rate",
    "loss_reduction", "sample_size", "configuration"
  ),
  selected_value = c(
    selected_parameters$mtry,
    selected_parameters$trees,
    selected_parameters$min_n,
    selected_parameters$tree_depth,
    selected_parameters$learn_rate,
    selected_parameters$loss_reduction,
    selected_parameters$sample_size,
    selected_parameters$.config
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  selected_display,
  digits = 5,
  caption = "Parameters locked for final full-data training"
)

tuning_finding <- data.frame(
  finding = c(
    "Untuned mean ROC-AUC on tuning folds",
    "Best tuned mean ROC-AUC on tuning folds",
    "Same-fold tuning change",
    "Tuning improved the same-fold control"
  ),
  result = c(
    sprintf("%.4f", untuned_tuning_auc),
    sprintf("%.4f", best_tuning_auc),
    sprintf("%+.4f ROC-AUC", best_tuning_auc - untuned_tuning_auc),
    ifelse(best_tuning_auc > untuned_tuning_auc, "Yes", "No")
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  tuning_finding,
  caption = "Randomized-tuning finding"
)
```

The selected configuration is now locked. It will be used without further search when the final model is trained on the complete training population. The 5K tuning estimate is useful for relative parameter selection but remains less precise than a full-data validation estimate.

**Implications**
