`r if (best_tuning_auc > untuned_tuning_auc) sprintf("On the same 5K tuning folds, randomized tuning improves mean ROC-AUC by %+.4f; the selected settings therefore merit confirmation on the full-data folds.", best_tuning_auc - untuned_tuning_auc) else sprintf("Randomized tuning changes mean ROC-AUC by %+.4f and does not beat the untuned control, so the untuned settings remain the stronger provisional choice.", best_tuning_auc - untuned_tuning_auc)` The small tuning sample is used for efficient parameter selection, not as final performance evidence.

**Takeaway from Section 7:** `r if (best_tuning_auc > untuned_tuning_auc) "The tuning search found a promising configuration, but full-data confirmation is required before selection." else "The randomized search did not justify replacing the untuned configuration."`

# Section 8: Full-data confirmation of the tuned candidate

**Purpose**

This section applies the locked Section 7 parameters without further search and measures the locked workflow on the established full-data folds. Because model selection occurs only after this confirmation, the tuned workflow is not fitted separately on all 307,511 rows unless it wins the comparison.

**Connection:** The small-sample tuning result is returned to the full-data folds here so model selection rests on the stronger validation population.

The full-data confirmation is useful because the tuning sample is intentionally small. It is not described as a fully independent nested-CV estimate: the 5K tuning applicants come from the same development population and can appear in the established folds.

**Method**

## Locked XGBoost workflow

```{r}
#| label: define-locked-workflow

locked_xgboost_spec <- parsnip::boost_tree(
  mtry = as.integer(selected_parameters$mtry),
  trees = as.integer(selected_parameters$trees),
  min_n = as.integer(selected_parameters$min_n),
  tree_depth = as.integer(selected_parameters$tree_depth),
  learn_rate = selected_parameters$learn_rate,
  loss_reduction = selected_parameters$loss_reduction,
  sample_size = selected_parameters$sample_size
) |>
  parsnip::set_engine(
    "xgboost",
    nthread = resample_engine_threads,
    verbosity = 0
  ) |>
  parsnip::set_mode("classification")

locked_workflow <- workflows::workflow() |>
  workflows::add_recipe(full_history_recipe) |>
  workflows::add_model(locked_xgboost_spec)

locked_specification <- data.frame(
  parameter = c(
    "mtry", "trees", "min_n", "tree_depth", "learn_rate",
    "loss_reduction", "sample_size", "imbalance strategy",
    "feature set"
  ),
  value = c(
    selected_parameters$mtry,
    selected_parameters$trees,
    selected_parameters$min_n,
    selected_parameters$tree_depth,
    selected_parameters$learn_rate,
    selected_parameters$loss_reduction,
    selected_parameters$sample_size,
    "Unadjusted",
    "Application plus supplementary history"
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  locked_specification,
  digits = 5,
  caption = "Locked final-workflow specification"
)
```

`r if (identical(best_imbalance_strategy$model, "XGBoost — unadjusted")) "The imbalance strategy remains unadjusted because none of the tested Section 6 alternatives improved mean ROC-AUC." else sprintf("The confirmation carries forward %s because it had the highest Section 6 mean ROC-AUC.", best_imbalance_strategy$model)` The recipe remains fold-safe during confirmation. Only the model selected from the confirmation evidence will later be fitted on all training rows.

**Results**

## Full-data post-tuning confirmation

```{r}
#| label: confirm-locked-full-data

locked_spec_signature <- digest::digest(list(
  seed = model_seed,
  model = locked_xgboost_spec,
  selected_parameters = selected_parameters,
  features = feature_manifests$full,
  fold_ids = modeling_cv_folds$id
))

locked_confirmation <- cached_modeling_result("locked_full_confirmation", run_candidate_model(
  model_label = "Locked tuned XGBoost — full history",
  model_spec = locked_xgboost_spec,
  recipe = full_history_recipe,
  folds = modeling_cv_folds,
  metrics = comparison_metrics,
  seed = model_seed
), spec_signature = locked_spec_signature)

locked_confirmation_summary <- locked_confirmation$metrics |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$.metric) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    mean = mean(.data$.estimate),
    std_dev = stats::sd(.data$.estimate),
    std_error = stats::sd(.data$.estimate) / sqrt(dplyr::n()),
    folds = dplyr::n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

locked_auc <- locked_confirmation_summary$mean[
  locked_confirmation_summary$.metric == "roc_auc"
]
locked_auc_se <- locked_confirmation_summary$std_error[
  locked_confirmation_summary$.metric == "roc_auc"
]

full_data_confirmation <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(
    model = "Untuned XGBoost — full history",
    mean_roc_auc = unname(
      auc_lookup["XGBoost — full history"]
    ),
    std_error = auc_comparison$std_error[
      auc_comparison$model == "XGBoost — full history"
    ],
    folds = 3L
  ),
  data.frame(
    model = "Locked tuned XGBoost — full history",
    mean_roc_auc = locked_auc,
    std_error = locked_auc_se,
    folds = 3L
  )
)

confirmation_checks <- c(
  "Locked confirmation lacks three folds" = all(
    table(locked_confirmation$metrics$id) == 2L
  ) && length(unique(locked_confirmation$metrics$id)) == 3L,
  "Locked confirmation produced an error note" =
    !nrow(locked_confirmation$notes) ||
      !any(locked_confirmation$notes$type == "error"),
  "Locked confirmation ROC-AUC is invalid" =
    is.finite(locked_auc) && locked_auc >= 0 && locked_auc <= 1
)

if (!all(confirmation_checks)) {
  stop(
    "Full-data confirmation failed: ",
    paste(names(confirmation_checks)[!confirmation_checks], collapse = "; ")
  )
}

knitr::kable(
  full_data_confirmation,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Untuned and locked tuned XGBoost on established full-data folds"
)
```

The confirmation comparison shows whether the parameter pattern selected on 5,000 rows transfers to the complete development population. The settings remain locked regardless of this result; no second search is conducted on the full folds.

## Retain the tuned audit record without a full-data fit

```{r}
#| label: save-tuned-cv-record

model_dir <- file.path(project_root, "models")
dir.create(model_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
tuned_cv_record_path <- file.path(model_dir, "tuned_xgboost_cv_record.rds")

verification_data <- train_modeling_base[seq_len(100L), , drop = FALSE]

tuned_cv_record <- list(
  model_name = "Home Credit locked tuned XGBoost candidate",
  disposition = "Not selected; no separate full-data model fit",
  parameters = as.list(selected_parameters),
  tuning_sample_cv = same_fold_comparison,
  full_data_cv = full_data_confirmation,
  full_data_fold_metrics = locked_confirmation$metrics,
  seed = model_seed,
  modeling_spec_signature = locked_spec_signature,
  validation_folds = 3L,
  tuning_sample_rows = nrow(tuning_sample),
  tuning_configurations = nrow(tuning_grid)
)
saveRDS(tuned_cv_record, tuned_cv_record_path)

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    retained_item = c(
      "Locked tuned parameters",
      "5K tuning-fold comparison",
      "Full-data 3-fold confirmation",
      "Separate full-data fitted workflow"
    ),
    status = c("Retained", "Retained", "Retained", "Not created")
  ),
  caption = "Tuned-candidate audit record"
)
```

The compact audit record preserves the tuned parameters and both levels of cross-validation evidence. It does not contain a fitted XGBoost workflow, avoiding an unnecessary full-data fit and duplicate model artifact.

**Implications**

`r if (locked_auc > unname(auc_lookup["XGBoost — full history"])) sprintf("The locked tuned model improves full-data mean ROC-AUC by %+.4f and is supported for final selection.", locked_auc - unname(auc_lookup["XGBoost — full history"])) else sprintf("The locked tuned model trails the untuned full-history XGBoost by %+.4f ROC-AUC, so tuning-sample gains do not transfer to the full development population.", locked_auc - unname(auc_lookup["XGBoost — full history"]))` Its parameters and CV evidence remain auditable, but no unselected full-data workflow is fitted or saved.

**Takeaway from Section 8:** `r if (locked_auc > unname(auc_lookup["XGBoost — full history"])) "The tuned configuration is supported by full-data confirmation." else "The tuned configuration is not supported by full-data confirmation; final selection also considers the native-missing experiment."`

# Section 9: Final selection and business interpretation

**Purpose**

This section connects the validation evidence to a final model choice and translates out-of-fold predictions into risk concentration, calibration, and feature-importance evidence that the business can interpret without treating the model as an approval policy.

**Connection:** The full-data comparison from Section 8 determines which workflow is interpreted and preserved as the selected model.

**Method**

## Final model decision

`r if (best_tuning_auc > untuned_tuning_auc) sprintf("The 5K tuning exercise improved mean ROC-AUC by %+.4f over the untuned control on the same small tuning folds.", best_tuning_auc - untuned_tuning_auc) else sprintf("The 5K tuning exercise changed mean ROC-AUC by %+.4f and did not improve over the untuned control on the same small tuning folds.", best_tuning_auc - untuned_tuning_auc)` On the established full-data folds, locked tuned XGBoost achieved ROC-AUC `r sprintf("%.4f", locked_auc)`, compared with `r sprintf("%.4f", unname(auc_lookup["XGBoost — full history"]))` for untuned full-history XGBoost. The fold-mean value differs slightly from the pooled out-of-fold ROC-AUC reported below because one averages three fold statistics while the other calculates one statistic over all out-of-fold predictions.

The final selection therefore follows the strongest full-data validation evidence. The selected model uses the untuned full-history XGBoost specification with native numeric missing-value routing. The tuned parameters and CV results remain saved in a compact audit record; no unselected tuned workflow is fitted on all rows.

```{r}
#| label: select-final-validated-model

# Selection is guarded by full-data CV rather than the smaller tuning-sample result.
stopifnot(
  "Native-missing XGBoost must outperform both imputed and locked tuned alternatives" =
    native_missing_auc > unname(auc_lookup["XGBoost — full history"]) &&
      native_missing_auc > locked_auc
)

selected_model_parameters <- list(
  mtry = 100L,
  trees = 300L,
  min_n = 10L,
  tree_depth = 6L,
  learn_rate = 0.05,
  loss_reduction = 0,
  sample_size = 0.8
)

selected_xgboost_spec <- parsnip::boost_tree(
  mtry = selected_model_parameters$mtry,
  trees = selected_model_parameters$trees,
  min_n = selected_model_parameters$min_n,
  tree_depth = selected_model_parameters$tree_depth,
  learn_rate = selected_model_parameters$learn_rate,
  loss_reduction = selected_model_parameters$loss_reduction,
  sample_size = selected_model_parameters$sample_size
) |>
  parsnip::set_engine("xgboost", nthread = 4, verbosity = 0) |>
  parsnip::set_mode("classification")

selected_workflow <- workflows::workflow() |>
  workflows::add_recipe(native_missing_recipe) |>
  workflows::add_model(selected_xgboost_spec)

selected_model_spec_signature <- digest::digest(list(
  seed = model_seed,
  model = selected_xgboost_spec,
  parameters = selected_model_parameters,
  missing_strategy = "native_xgboost",
  features = feature_manifests$full
))

selection_summary <- data.frame(
  candidate = c(
    "Untuned full-history XGBoost — native missing",
    "Untuned full-history XGBoost",
    "5K-tuned full-history XGBoost"
  ),
  full_data_cv_roc_auc = c(
    native_missing_auc,
    unname(auc_lookup["XGBoost — full history"]),
    locked_auc
  ),
  std_error = c(
    native_missing_auc_se,
    auc_comparison$std_error[
      auc_comparison$model == "XGBoost — full history"
    ],
    locked_auc_se
  ),
  disposition = c(
    "Selected",
    "Not selected",
    "Retained as tuning audit artifact"
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  selection_summary,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Final model selection based on full-data cross-validation"
)
```

This choice does not invalidate the tuning exercise. It documents that a parameter pattern found on 5,000 rows was not sufficiently stable when evaluated across the full development population.

**Results**

## Out-of-fold predictions for the selected model

```{r}
#| label: selected-model-oof-predictions

selected_oof <- list(
  model = "Selected native-missing full-history XGBoost",
  metrics = native_missing_run$metrics,
  predictions = native_missing_run$predictions,
  notes = native_missing_run$notes,
  elapsed_seconds = native_missing_run$elapsed_seconds
)

oof_predictions <- selected_oof$predictions
probability_column <- ".pred_payment_difficulty"

required_oof_columns <- c(".row", "TARGET", probability_column, "id")
if (!all(required_oof_columns %in% names(oof_predictions))) {
  stop("Out-of-fold predictions lack required columns.")
}

oof_predictions$SK_ID_CURR <- train_modeling_base$SK_ID_CURR[
  oof_predictions$.row
]

oof_checks <- c(
  "Out-of-fold prediction count differs from training" =
    nrow(oof_predictions) == nrow(train_modeling_base),
  "An applicant lacks an out-of-fold prediction" = setequal(
    oof_predictions$SK_ID_CURR,
    train_modeling_base$SK_ID_CURR
  ),
  "An applicant has multiple out-of-fold predictions" =
    !anyDuplicated(oof_predictions$SK_ID_CURR),
  "Out-of-fold probabilities contain missing values" =
    !anyNA(oof_predictions[[probability_column]]),
  "Out-of-fold probabilities fall outside 0–1" = all(
    oof_predictions[[probability_column]] >= 0 &
      oof_predictions[[probability_column]] <= 1
  )
)

if (!all(oof_checks)) {
  stop(
    "Out-of-fold prediction validation failed: ",
    paste(names(oof_checks)[!oof_checks], collapse = "; ")
  )
}

selected_oof_auc <- yardstick::roc_auc_vec(
  truth = oof_predictions$TARGET,
  estimate = oof_predictions[[probability_column]],
  event_level = "first"
)

stopifnot(
  "Sections 9–10 and the Conclusion require supplementary history to improve XGBoost" =
    xgboost_supplementary_auc_change > 0,
  "Sections 9–10 and the Conclusion require the selected model to remain below 0.79" =
    selected_oof_auc < 0.79
)

if (abs(selected_oof_auc - native_missing_auc) > 0.0005) {
  stop("Reproduced out-of-fold ROC-AUC differs from the selected-model estimate.")
}

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    check = c(
      "Applicants with one out-of-fold probability",
      "Reproduced ROC-AUC",
      "Fitting errors"
    ),
    result = c(
      format(nrow(oof_predictions), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE),
      sprintf("%.4f", selected_oof_auc),
      "None"
    )
  ),
  caption = "Selected-model out-of-fold validation"
)
```

Every probability above comes from a model that did not train on that applicant. These predictions support the ranking and calibration summaries below without substituting optimistic in-sample results.

## Risk concentration by out-of-fold decile

```{r}
#| label: oof-risk-deciles

risk_deciles <- oof_predictions |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    event = .data$TARGET == payment_difficulty_level,
    risk_decile = dplyr::ntile(.data[[probability_column]], 10L)
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$risk_decile) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    applicants = dplyr::n(),
    events = sum(.data$event),
    mean_predicted_risk = mean(.data[[probability_column]]),
    observed_event_rate = mean(.data$event),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(.data$risk_decile)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    event_capture = .data$events / sum(.data$events),
    cumulative_event_capture = cumsum(.data$events) / sum(.data$events),
    risk_label = paste0("Decile ", .data$risk_decile)
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    .data$risk_label,
    .data$applicants,
    .data$events,
    .data$mean_predicted_risk,
    .data$observed_event_rate,
    .data$event_capture,
    .data$cumulative_event_capture
  )

knitr::kable(
  risk_deciles,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Out-of-fold risk concentration from highest to lowest predicted decile",
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
)
```

`r sprintf("If review capacity were limited to the highest-risk 10%% of applicants, the model would identify %.2f%% of observed payment-difficulty cases; that reviewed group has an observed event rate of %.2f%%.", 100 * risk_deciles$event_capture[risk_deciles$risk_label == "Decile 10"], 100 * risk_deciles$observed_event_rate[risk_deciles$risk_label == "Decile 10"])`

The deciles describe ranking, not approval bands. They show how effectively the model concentrates observed payment difficulty among applicants assigned higher risk, which can support review prioritization or policy simulation once decision costs and risk appetite are supplied.

## Calibration diagnostics

```{r}
#| label: oof-calibration

selected_brier <- yardstick::brier_class_vec(
  truth = oof_predictions$TARGET,
  estimate = oof_predictions[[probability_column]],
  event_level = "first"
)

observed_rate <- mean(
  oof_predictions$TARGET == payment_difficulty_level
)
mean_predicted_rate <- mean(oof_predictions[[probability_column]])
constant_prevalence_brier <- observed_rate * (1 - observed_rate)

calibration_summary <- data.frame(
  diagnostic = c(
    "Observed payment-difficulty rate",
    "Mean predicted probability",
    "Selected-model Brier score",
    "Constant-prevalence Brier score"
  ),
  value = c(
    observed_rate,
    mean_predicted_rate,
    selected_brier,
    constant_prevalence_brier
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  calibration_summary,
  digits = 5,
  caption = "Out-of-fold probability calibration diagnostics"
)
```

ROC-AUC measures ranking, while the Brier score measures squared probability error. The decile table provides the more detailed calibration view by comparing average predictions with observed outcomes across risk levels. A later production process should monitor both discrimination and calibration because portfolio mix and policy can change over time.

**Finalization method**

## Fit and preserve the selected final workflow

```{r}
#| label: fit-save-selected-workflow

selected_model_path <- file.path(model_dir, "selected_xgboost_workflow.rds")
selected_metadata_path <- file.path(model_dir, "selected_xgboost_metadata.rds")

selected_metadata_input <- list(
  model_name = "Home Credit selected native-missing full-history XGBoost",
  selection_reason = paste(
    "Highest established full-data cross-validated ROC-AUC among evaluated models"
  ),
  outcome = "TARGET",
  event_level = payment_difficulty_level,
  id_column = "SK_ID_CURR",
  feature_set = "application_plus_supplementary_history",
  missing_value_strategy = "native_xgboost_routing",
  imbalance_strategy = "unadjusted",
  seed = model_seed,
  modeling_spec_signature = selected_model_spec_signature,
  model_parameters = selected_model_parameters,
  full_cv_roc_auc = selected_oof_auc,
  full_cv_roc_auc_std_error = native_missing_auc_se,
  brier_score = selected_brier,
  validation_folds = 3L
)

saved_selected_metadata <- if (file.exists(selected_metadata_path)) {
  readRDS(selected_metadata_path)
} else {
  NULL
}
saved_selected_spec_matches <-
  is.list(saved_selected_metadata) &&
  identical(
    saved_selected_metadata$model_parameters,
    selected_model_parameters
  ) &&
  identical(
    saved_selected_metadata$modeling_spec_signature,
    selected_model_spec_signature
  ) &&
  identical(saved_selected_metadata$seed, model_seed)

if (identical(modeling_run_mode, "development") &&
    file.exists(selected_model_path) &&
    saved_selected_spec_matches) {
  selected_model_result <- load_verify_final_workflow(
    model_path = selected_model_path,
    metadata_path = selected_metadata_path,
    verification_data = verification_data
  )
} else {
  selected_model_result <- fit_save_verify_final_workflow(
    workflow = selected_workflow,
    training_data = train_modeling_base,
    verification_data = verification_data,
    model_path = selected_model_path,
    metadata_path = selected_metadata_path,
    metadata = selected_metadata_input
  )
}

selected_recipe_fitted <- workflows::extract_recipe(
  selected_model_result$fitted_workflow
)
selected_roles <- summary(selected_recipe_fitted)
selected_predictors <- selected_roles$variable[
  selected_roles$role == "predictor"
]

selected_artifact_checks <- c(
  selected_model_result$checks,
  "Selected model ID entered predictors" =
    !"SK_ID_CURR" %in% selected_predictors,
  "Selected model outcome entered predictors" =
    !"TARGET" %in% selected_predictors,
  "Selected model predictor matrix is empty" =
    length(selected_predictors) > 0
)

if (!all(selected_artifact_checks)) {
  stop(
    "Selected-model artifact validation failed: ",
    paste(names(selected_artifact_checks)[!selected_artifact_checks], collapse = "; ")
  )
}
```

Section 8 preserves the unselected tuned candidate as a compact CV record, while this section saves the only fitted full-data workflow. This preserves the modeling decision trail without maintaining a duplicate unselected model.

**Final-model results**

## Predictive importance

```{r}
#| label: selected-feature-importance

selected_engine <- workflows::extract_fit_parsnip(
  selected_model_result$fitted_workflow
)$fit

feature_importance <- xgboost::xgb.importance(model = selected_engine)
feature_importance$theme <- classify_feature_theme(feature_importance$Feature)

top_feature_importance <- feature_importance |>
  dplyr::slice_max(order_by = .data$Gain, n = 20, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::select(.data$Feature, .data$theme, .data$Gain, .data$Cover, .data$Frequency)

theme_importance <- feature_importance |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$theme) |>
  dplyr::summarise(gain = sum(.data$Gain), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(.data$gain))

knitr::kable(
  top_feature_importance,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Top selected-model predictors by XGBoost gain"
)

knitr::kable(
  theme_importance,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Predictive gain grouped by business-oriented feature theme"
)
```

Gain measures how much tree splits using a field improve the XGBoost objective. It does not establish a causal relationship, a favorable or unfavorable direction, or whether changing the field would change payment outcomes. Anonymized external scores also remain less explainable than directly interpretable repayment-history measures.

## Business and performance conclusion

```{r}
#| label: business-performance-summary

top_decile_event_rate <- risk_deciles$observed_event_rate[
  risk_deciles$risk_label == "Decile 10"
]
top_decile_capture <- risk_deciles$event_capture[
  risk_deciles$risk_label == "Decile 10"
]

business_summary <- data.frame(
  result = c(
    "Majority-class ROC-AUC",
    "Simple-logistic ROC-AUC",
    "Selected-model ROC-AUC",
    "Improvement over simple logistic",
    "Project ROC-AUC target",
    "Target reached",
    "Highest-risk decile observed event rate",
    "Events captured in highest-risk decile"
  ),
  value = c(
    sprintf("%.4f", majority_auc),
    sprintf("%.4f", logistic_auc),
    sprintf("%.4f", selected_oof_auc),
    sprintf("%+.4f", selected_oof_auc - logistic_auc),
    "0.7900",
    ifelse(selected_oof_auc >= 0.79, "Yes", "No"),
    sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * top_decile_event_rate),
    sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * top_decile_capture)
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  business_summary,
  caption = "Selected-model performance and business-facing ranking summary"
)

selected_artifacts <- data.frame(
  artifact = c("Selected fitted workflow", "Selected model metadata"),
  file = c(basename(selected_model_path), basename(selected_metadata_path)),
  size_megabytes = round(
    file.info(c(selected_model_path, selected_metadata_path))$size / 1024^2,
    2
  ),
  read_test = "Passed"
)

knitr::kable(
  selected_artifacts,
  caption = "Selected-model artifacts"
)
```

The selected model materially improves risk ranking over both the majority classifier and simple logistic benchmark, and the supplementary-feature experiment shows that historical information adds incremental value. It does not reach the project's 0.79 ROC-AUC target, so that gap is reported rather than obscured.

The model can support ranking applicants for additional review or policy simulation. It cannot by itself determine approvals. The supplied data do not contain rejected applicants, complete decision costs, pricing, recovery, or an approved risk threshold, and the model was developed on originated applications. Approval-rate lift and customer-impact claims therefore remain outside the evidence available here.

## Consolidated experiment registry

The registry below puts the benchmark, algorithm, feature-set, missing-data, imbalance, and tuning experiments in one place. Runtime is the elapsed time for the recorded resampling call and is therefore comparable only within this computing environment.

```{r}
#| label: consolidated-experiment-registry

# Attach candidate runtimes where available; benchmark runtimes were not recorded.
candidate_registry <- auc_comparison |>
  dplyr::left_join(candidate_runtime, by = "model") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    algorithm = dplyr::case_when(
      .data$model == "Majority class" ~ "Majority classifier",
      grepl("Ridge", .data$model) ~ "Ridge logistic",
      grepl("Random forest", .data$model) ~ "Random forest",
      grepl("XGBoost", .data$model) ~ "XGBoost",
      TRUE ~ "Logistic regression"
    ),
    feature_set = dplyr::case_when(
      grepl("application", .data$model, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Application only",
      .data$model == "Majority class" ~ "None",
      .data$model == "Simple logistic" ~ "Selected application predictors",
      TRUE ~ "Application + supplementary history"
    ),
    missing_strategy = dplyr::case_when(
      .data$model == "Simple logistic" ~ "Median + indicators",
      grepl("XGBoost|Ridge|Random forest", .data$model) ~
        "Median + indicators",
      TRUE ~ "Not applicable"
    ),
    imbalance_strategy = "Observed distribution",
    data_scope = "Full training; 3-fold CV",
    decision = dplyr::case_when(
      .data$model == "Majority class" ~ "No-skill benchmark",
      .data$model == "Simple logistic" ~ "Interpretable benchmark",
      .data$model == "XGBoost — full history" ~
        "Baseline for imbalance, tuning and missing-data experiments",
      TRUE ~ "Not advanced"
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    experiment = .data$model,
    .data$algorithm,
    .data$feature_set,
    .data$missing_strategy,
    .data$imbalance_strategy,
    .data$data_scope,
    cv_auc = .data$mean,
    std_error = .data$std_error,
    runtime_seconds = .data$elapsed_seconds,
    .data$decision
  )

adjusted_registry <- imbalance_comparison |>
  dplyr::filter(
    .data$.metric == "roc_auc",
    .data$model != "XGBoost — unadjusted"
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(imbalance_runtime, by = "model") |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    experiment = .data$model,
    algorithm = "XGBoost",
    feature_set = "Application + supplementary history",
    missing_strategy = "Median + indicators",
    imbalance_strategy = sub("XGBoost — ", "", .data$model),
    data_scope = "Full training; 3-fold CV",
    cv_auc = .data$mean,
    std_error = .data$std_error,
    runtime_seconds = .data$elapsed_seconds,
    decision = "Rejected; did not improve ranking"
  )

additional_registry <- data.frame(
  experiment = c(
    "XGBoost — full history, native missing",
    "Best randomized XGBoost configuration",
    "Locked tuned XGBoost — full confirmation"
  ),
  algorithm = "XGBoost",
  feature_set = "Application + supplementary history",
  missing_strategy = c(
    "Native XGBoost routing",
    "Median + indicators",
    "Median + indicators"
  ),
  imbalance_strategy = "Observed distribution",
  data_scope = c(
    "Full training; 3-fold CV",
    "5K tuning sample; 3-fold CV",
    "Full training; 3-fold CV"
  ),
  cv_auc = c(native_missing_auc, best_tuning_auc, locked_auc),
  std_error = c(native_missing_auc_se, best_tuning_se, locked_auc_se),
  runtime_seconds = c(
    native_missing_run$elapsed_seconds,
    tuning_run$elapsed_seconds,
    locked_confirmation$elapsed_seconds
  ),
  decision = c(
    "Selected and fitted on all training rows",
    "Advanced to full-data confirmation",
    "Rejected after full-data confirmation"
  )
)

experiment_registry <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  candidate_registry,
  adjusted_registry,
  additional_registry
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    scope_order = ifelse(
      .data$data_scope == "5K tuning sample; 3-fold CV",
      2L,
      1L
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(.data$scope_order, dplyr::desc(.data$cv_auc)) |>
  dplyr::select(-.data$scope_order)

knitr::kable(
  experiment_registry,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Consolidated modeling experiment registry",
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
)
```

The 5K tuning-sample row is placed after all full-training experiments because its ROC-AUC is suitable for within-sample parameter selection but is not directly comparable with full-data cross-validation estimates.

**Implications**

`r if (selected_oof_auc > logistic_auc) sprintf("The selected model improves pooled out-of-fold ROC-AUC by %+.4f over simple logistic and captures %.2f%% of observed payment difficulties in the highest-risk decile.", selected_oof_auc - logistic_auc, 100 * top_decile_capture) else sprintf("The selected model does not improve on the simple logistic benchmark; its ROC-AUC difference is %+.4f.", selected_oof_auc - logistic_auc)` `r if (selected_brier < constant_prevalence_brier) sprintf("Its Brier score of %.5f also improves on the constant-prevalence reference of %.5f.", selected_brier, constant_prevalence_brier) else sprintf("Its Brier score of %.5f does not improve on the constant-prevalence reference of %.5f.", selected_brier, constant_prevalence_brier)` These results support prioritization for review, not an automatic approval threshold.

**Takeaway from Section 9:** `r if (selected_oof_auc >= 0.79) "The selected model reaches the project discrimination target and provides useful risk concentration, subject to governance review." else "The selected model improves materially on the benchmarks and concentrates risk usefully, but it does not reach the 0.79 project target."`

# Section 10: Governance, limitations, and conclusion

## Carried-forward items from data preparation

The data-preparation notebook identified several choices that required explicit closure during modeling. The table below records their disposition so unresolved assumptions are not lost between phases.

| Carried-forward item | Modeling disposition | Remaining limitation or evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Raw, `log1p`, and capped amount representations | Not separately ablated for the selected tree model. All were retained in the full-history recipe. For trees, `log1p` preserves the exact split ordering of positive raw amounts, while capped copies differ only in the tails; XGBoost can ignore redundant versions through split selection. | This rationale is specific to the tree model. A formal ablation was not run, so the notebook does not claim that all three representations are independently valuable. |
| `OWN_CAR_AGE_GT50` sensitivity | The plausibility flag remained an approved predictor, but a with/without sensitivity comparison was not run. | Treat as an unclosed robustness test before production use; inspect dependence and subgroup effects if the feature is materially important. |
| NULL payment-date shortfall interpretation | The preparation rule was carried into installment aggregates and evaluated only as part of the complete supplementary feature set. | The meaning of a NULL payment date was not independently validated. Rebuild the installment features under an alternative interpretation as a sensitivity test when source-system documentation is available. |
| `DAYS_EMPLOYED_SENTINEL` proxy overlap | The sentinel remained a predictor while age and organization fields remained audit-only. See the subgroup table for computed age-band performance. | The audit does not isolate the sentinel's incremental subgroup effect. Its overlap with pensioner/age information remains a proxy-governance concern requiring a targeted with/without review. |
| Native-missing experiment sequencing | Class-imbalance and tuning experiments used the median-imputation recipe as their common baseline; they were not repeated after native missing routing won the final ablation. | The final selection compares both missing-data strategies on the established folds, but interactions between native missing routing, imbalance handling, and tuning remain untested. |
| Explicit missingness indicators from EDA Q7/Q10 | Explicit indicators, including the `EXT_SOURCE_1` indicator used to document train/test shift, remain in benchmark and comparison models. The selected XGBoost model instead learns missingness implicitly through split routing. | Continue monitoring source-level missingness explicitly outside the final predictor matrix; native routing does not replace data-quality and population-shift monitoring. |

These items do not invalidate the reported cross-validation results. They limit how confidently individual engineered fields can be defended or transferred into production.

## Subgroup monitoring audit

The EDA retained sensitive and proxy fields for auditing rather than prediction. This section joins those fields to the selected model's out-of-fold probabilities using `SK_ID_CURR`. It examines gender, age bands, and current contract type as monitoring dimensions.

ROC-AUC and Brier score are suppressed for groups with fewer than 1,000 applicants or 100 observed payment-difficulty cases. The thresholds prevent very small groups from producing apparently precise performance estimates. They are analytical stability rules, not legal safe harbors or definitions of fairness.

```{r}
#| label: subgroup-performance-audit

audit_match <- match(
  oof_predictions$SK_ID_CURR,
  train_modeling_base$SK_ID_CURR
)

if (anyNA(audit_match)) {
  stop("Out-of-fold applicants could not be matched to audit fields.")
}

subgroup_data <- data.frame(
  SK_ID_CURR = oof_predictions$SK_ID_CURR,
  TARGET = oof_predictions$TARGET,
  .pred_payment_difficulty = oof_predictions[[probability_column]],
  CODE_GENDER = train_modeling_base$CODE_GENDER[audit_match],
  age_years = train_modeling_base$age_years[audit_match],
  NAME_CONTRACT_TYPE = train_modeling_base$NAME_CONTRACT_TYPE[audit_match],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

subgroup_data$age_band <- cut(
  subgroup_data$age_years,
  breaks = c(-Inf, 24, 34, 44, 54, 64, Inf),
  labels = c("Under 25", "25–34", "35–44", "45–54", "55–64", "65+"),
  right = TRUE
)

subgroup_audit <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(
  c("CODE_GENDER", "age_band", "NAME_CONTRACT_TYPE"),
  function(field) {
    summarize_subgroup_performance(
      subgroup_data,
      group_col = field,
      min_applicants = 1000L,
      min_events = 100L
    )
  }
))

subgroup_checks <- c(
  "Subgroup audit lost applicants" =
    nrow(subgroup_data) == nrow(oof_predictions),
  "Subgroup audit contains missing probabilities" =
    !anyNA(subgroup_data$.pred_payment_difficulty),
  "An undersized group was reported" = !any(
    subgroup_audit$performance_status == "Reported" &
      (subgroup_audit$applicants < 1000L | subgroup_audit$events < 100L)
  )
)

reported_subgroup_audit <- subgroup_audit |>
  dplyr::filter(
    .data$performance_status == "Reported",
    is.finite(.data$roc_auc)
  )
subgroup_auc_min <- if (nrow(reported_subgroup_audit)) {
  min(reported_subgroup_audit$roc_auc)
} else {
  NA_real_
}
subgroup_auc_max <- if (nrow(reported_subgroup_audit)) {
  max(reported_subgroup_audit$roc_auc)
} else {
  NA_real_
}

if (!all(subgroup_checks)) {
  stop(
    "Subgroup audit validation failed: ",
    paste(names(subgroup_checks)[!subgroup_checks], collapse = "; ")
  )
}

knitr::kable(
  subgroup_audit,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Out-of-fold subgroup monitoring audit",
  format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
)
```

Differences in observed rates, average predictions, ROC-AUC, or Brier score identify groups that require further review. They do not prove discrimination, establish causation, or determine whether a model complies with the laws of any jurisdiction. A production governance process would also assess threshold-specific approval and error rates after an operating policy is proposed.

**Implications — subgroup audit:** `r if (nrow(reported_subgroup_audit) < 2L) "Too few subgroups meet the reporting thresholds to compare discrimination reliably; additional validation data are required." else if ((subgroup_auc_max - subgroup_auc_min) > 0.02) sprintf("Reported subgroup ROC-AUC ranges from %.4f to %.4f, a material spread of %.4f; targeted monitoring is warranted before a common operating threshold is considered.", subgroup_auc_min, subgroup_auc_max, subgroup_auc_max - subgroup_auc_min) else sprintf("Reported subgroup ROC-AUC ranges from %.4f to %.4f, a spread of %.4f; this gap is below the 0.02 monitoring trigger but should continue to be tracked.", subgroup_auc_min, subgroup_auc_max, subgroup_auc_max - subgroup_auc_min)` These descriptive differences are not, by themselves, a legal fairness conclusion.

knitr::kable(

The selected model beats both the no-skill classifier and the simple logistic benchmark, and historical information provides incremental predictive value. The 0.79 ROC-AUC project target was not reached. This is reported as a result rather than addressed through further unplanned searches that could overfit the development data.

## Limitations and governance controls

| Limitation or risk | Implication | Required next control |
|---|---|---|
| Originated-applicant development sample | The model may not represent rejected or future applicants | Validate on the intended applicant population and monitor population shift |
| No false-approval/false-decline cost ratio | ROC-AUC cannot determine an operating cutoff | Obtain stakeholder costs or an approved scenario range before threshold analysis |
| No complete approval policy, pricing, or recovery data | Approval-rate and profit lift cannot be estimated | Conduct policy simulation after those inputs are supplied |
| Anonymized external scores | Strong predictors are not fully explainable | Obtain provenance and reason-code support before production use |
| Sensitive and proxy fields | Group performance may differ even when fields are excluded | Continue subgroup calibration, error-rate, and outcome monitoring |
| Predictive feature importance | Importance is not causal direction or treatment effect | Use explanations only as predictive evidence; do not infer interventions |
| Random 3-fold validation | Does not measure temporal policy or economic drift | Add out-of-time validation when application dates or later cohorts are available |
| Payment-difficulty target | May not align with a regulatory default definition | Maintain the supplied target terminology and validate any regulatory mapping |

These limitations constrain how the model can be used. The current evidence supports risk ranking within a similar originated-applicant population. It does not support automatic approvals, adverse-action reasons, causal claims, or a quantified approval-rate lift.

## Generate and validate the submission file

```{r}
#| label: generate-validate-submission

sample_submission_path <- file.path(
  project_root, "data", "raw", "sample_submission.csv"
)
submission_path <- file.path(project_root, "outputs", "submission.csv")

sample_submission <- utils::read.csv(
  sample_submission_path,
  check.names = FALSE
)
selected_model_for_scoring <- readRDS(selected_model_path)
test_probabilities <- predict(
  selected_model_for_scoring,
  new_data = test_modeling_base,
  type = "prob"
)

scored_test <- data.frame(
  SK_ID_CURR = test_modeling_base$SK_ID_CURR,
  TARGET = test_probabilities$.pred_payment_difficulty
)
submission_match <- match(sample_submission$SK_ID_CURR, scored_test$SK_ID_CURR)

if (anyNA(submission_match)) {
  stop("One or more sample-submission IDs lack a model prediction.")
}

# Reorder predictions to the official template before writing the Kaggle CSV.
submission <- scored_test[submission_match, c("SK_ID_CURR", "TARGET")]
row.names(submission) <- NULL

if (!all(
  is.finite(submission$SK_ID_CURR) &
    submission$SK_ID_CURR == floor(submission$SK_ID_CURR)
)) {
  stop("Submission IDs must be finite whole numbers.")
}

# Format both numeric columns explicitly so R can never serialize a value with
# exponent notation (for example, writing ID 400000 as 4e+05).
submission_to_write <- data.frame(
  SK_ID_CURR = sprintf("%.0f", submission$SK_ID_CURR),
  TARGET = sprintf("%.17f", submission$TARGET),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
utils::write.table(
  submission_to_write,
  submission_path,
  sep = ",",
  row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = TRUE,
  quote = FALSE
)

submission_lines <- readLines(submission_path, warn = FALSE)
submission_has_scientific_notation <- any(grepl(
  "[eE][+-]?[0-9]+",
  submission_lines
))

submission_reloaded <- utils::read.csv(
  submission_path,
  check.names = FALSE
)

submission_checks <- c(
  "Submission file exists" = file.exists(submission_path),
  "Submission has required columns" = identical(
    names(submission_reloaded), c("SK_ID_CURR", "TARGET")
  ),
  "Submission has 48,744 rows" = nrow(submission_reloaded) == 48744L,
  "Submission IDs match the template order" = identical(
    as.numeric(submission_reloaded$SK_ID_CURR),
    as.numeric(sample_submission$SK_ID_CURR)
  ),
  "Submission IDs are unique" = !anyDuplicated(submission_reloaded$SK_ID_CURR),
  "Submission contains no scientific notation" =
    !submission_has_scientific_notation,
  "Submission probabilities are complete" = !anyNA(submission_reloaded$TARGET),
  "Submission probabilities are in [0, 1]" = all(
    submission_reloaded$TARGET >= 0 & submission_reloaded$TARGET <= 1
  )
)

if (!all(submission_checks)) {
  stop(
    "Submission validation failed: ",
    paste(names(submission_checks)[!submission_checks], collapse = "; ")
  )
}

knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    check = c(
      names(submission_checks),
      "Kaggle public score",
      "Kaggle private score"
    ),
    status = c(
      ifelse(submission_checks, "Passed", "Failed"),
      sprintf("%.5f", kaggle_public_score),
      sprintf("%.5f", kaggle_private_score)
    ),
    row.names = NULL
  ),
  caption = "Submission-file validation and Kaggle score status"
)
```

The generated file follows the provided template order and contains one probability for each of the 48,744 test applicants. Kaggle reported a public ROC-AUC of `r sprintf("%.5f", kaggle_public_score)` and a private ROC-AUC of `r sprintf("%.5f", kaggle_private_score)`.

**Implications — Kaggle result:** The public and private leaderboard scores provide external ranking evidence consistent with the local validation result, but they do not replace the cross-validation and governance evidence above.

**Takeaway from Section 10:** The model artifacts and submission file are reproducible, the Kaggle scores provide external ranking evidence, and subgroup variation and unresolved preparation sensitivities remain explicit governance or validation items.

## Use of AI

I used AI as a working partner throughout the modeling phase. It helped translate the modeling requirements into reusable R functions, fold-safe recipes, validation assertions, candidate workflows, randomized tuning, artifact checks, and notebook narrative. It also helped diagnose implementation issues, including the need for pre-recipe modeling tables, an oversized cache object, and lengthy tuning backtraces.

I reviewed the resulting decisions and outputs against the data map, industry context, EDA plan, data-preparation rules, and executed validation results. AI-generated suggestions were not accepted solely because they improved a metric. For example, imbalance adjustments were rejected when they reduced ROC-AUC, and the 5K-tuned model was not selected after it underperformed the untuned model on the established full-data folds.

# Conclusion

The project produced a reusable, fold-safe R modeling pipeline and a selected XGBoost model that improves payment-difficulty ranking over the required benchmarks. The model achieves a pooled out-of-fold ROC-AUC of `r sprintf("%.4f", selected_oof_auc)`, compared with `r sprintf("%.4f", logistic_auc)` for the simple logistic benchmark and `r sprintf("%.4f", majority_auc)` for the majority classifier. Applicants in the highest predicted-risk decile have a `r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * top_decile_event_rate)` observed payment-difficulty rate and account for `r sprintf("%.2f%%", 100 * top_decile_capture)` of all observed events.

Supplementary repayment and credit history adds measurable value, while explicit imbalance adjustments do not improve ranking for the tested XGBoost configuration. `r if (nrow(theme_importance) && identical(theme_importance$theme[1], "External risk score")) "External risk scores are the largest computed importance theme, creating an explainability dependency that requires additional governance before production use." else if (nrow(theme_importance)) sprintf("The largest computed importance theme is %s; its governance and explainability implications require review before production use.", theme_importance$theme[1]) else "No feature-importance theme was available for interpretation."`

The evidence supports prioritizing applicants for further risk review within a similar population. It does not support an approval threshold, causal conclusions, or approval-rate lift. Those decisions require stakeholder cost inputs, rejected-applicant data, policy simulation, and jurisdiction-specific governance review. The submission achieved Kaggle ROC-AUC scores of `r sprintf("%.5f", kaggle_public_score)` on the public leaderboard and `r sprintf("%.5f", kaggle_private_score)` on the private leaderboard.
